5.34 पित्र्यर्क्षं भगदैवत्यमुत्तरांश् च केसरी ।
सूर्यक्षेत्रं विभोर्ब्रह्मन् हृदयं परिगीयते ॥
5.m:
A portion of Āditya, and Puṣya, and Āśleṣā, the mansion of the Moon,
and the zodiac sign named Karkaṭaka are on the flanks of the destroyer of the sacrifice.

The ancestral constellation, that which has Bhaga for its deity, and the Uttarās, and Leo—
the domain of the Sun, O Brahmin, is proclaimed as the heart of the all-pervading Lord.

5.s:
uttarāṃśāstrayaḥ pāṇiścitrārdhaṃ kanyakā tviyam /
somaputrasya sadmaitad dvitīyaṃ jaṭharaṃ vibhoḥ //
5.d:
उत्तरांशास्त्रयः पाणिश्चित्रार्धं कन्यका त्वियम् ।
सोमपुत्रस्य सद्मैतद् द्वितीयं जठरं विभोः ॥
5.m: Three parts of Uttaraphalgunī, Hasta, and half of Citrā are Virgo; / this is the second abode of the Son of the Moon, the belly of the all-pervading Lord.

5.s:
citrāṃśadvitayaṃ svātirviśākhāyāṃśakatrayam /
dvitīyaṃ sukrasadanaṃ tulā nābhirudāhṛtā //
5.d:
चित्रांशद्वितयं स्वातिर्विशाखायांशकत्रयम् ।
द्वितीयं सुक्रसदनं तुला नाभिरुदाहृता ॥
5.m: Two parts of Citrā, Svātī, and three parts of Viśākhā / are the second abode of Venus, Libra, declared to be his navel.

5.s:
viśākhāṃśamanūrādhā jyeṣṭhā bhaumagṛhaṃ tvidam /
dvitīyaṃ vṛściko rāśirmeḍhraṃ kālasavarūpiṇaḥ //
5.d:
विशाखांशमनूराधा ज्येष्ठा भौमगृहं त्विदम् ।
द्वितीयं वृश्चिको राशिर्मेढ्रं कालसवरूपिणः ॥
5.m: One part of Viśākhā, Anurādhā, and Jyeṣṭhā are this house of Mars, / the second, the sign Scorpio, the penis of the one whose form is Time.

5.s:
mūlaṃ pūrvottarāṃśaśca devācajāryagṛhaṃ dhanuḥ /
ūruyugalamīśasya amararṣe pragīyate //
5.d:
मूलं पूर्वोत्तरांशश्च देवाचजार्यगृहं धनुः ।
ऊरुयुगलमीशस्य अमरर्षे प्रगीयते ॥
5.m: Mūla and the parts of Pūrvāṣāḍhā and Uttarāṣāḍhā, the house of the preceptor of the gods, Sagittarius, / is sung, O celestial sage, as the pair of thighs of the Lord.

5.s:
uttarāṃśāstrayo ṛkṣaṃ śravaṇaṃ makaro mune /
dhaniṣṭhārdhaṃ śatabhiṣā jānunī parameṣṭhinaḥ //
5.d:
उत्तरांशास्त्रयो ऋक्षं श्रवणं मकरो मुने ।
धनिष्ठार्धं शतभिषा जानुनी परमेष्ठिनः ॥
5.m: Three parts of Uttarāṣāḍhā, the asterism Śravaṇa, is Capricorn, O sage; / half of Dhaniṣṭhā and Śatabhiṣā are the knees of the Supreme Lord.

5.s:
dhaniṣṭhārdhaṃ śatabhiṣā prauṣṭhapadyāṃśakatrayam /
saureḥ sadmāparamidaṃ kumbho jaṅghe ca viśrate //
5.d:
धनिष्ठार्धं शतभिषा प्रौष्ठपद्यांशकत्रयम् ।
सौरेः सद्मापरमिदं कुम्भो जङ्घे च विश्रते ॥
5.m: Half of Dhaniṣṭhā, Śatabhiṣā, and three parts of Pūrvabhādrapadā / are this second abode of Saturn, Aquarius, known as his shanks.

5.s:
proṣṭhapadyāṃśamekaṃ tu uttarā revatī tathā /
dvitīyaṃ jīvasadanaṃ mīnastu caraṇāvubhau //
5.d:
प्रोष्ठपद्यांशमेकं तु उत्तरा रेवती तथा ।
द्वितीयं जीवसदनं मीनस्तु चरणावुभौ ॥
5.m: One part of Pūrvabhādrapadā, Uttarabhādrapadā, and Revatī / are the second abode of Jupiter; Pisces forms both of his feet.

5.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā kālarūpaṃ trinetro yajñaṃ krodhānmārgarājaghāna /
viddhaścāsau vedanābuddhimuktaḥ khe saṃtasthau tārakābhiścitāṅgaḥ //
5.d:
एवं कृत्वा कालरूपं त्रिनेत्रो यज्ञं क्रोधान्मार्गराजघान ।
विद्धश्चासौ वेदनाबुद्धिमुक्तः खे संतस्थौ तारकाभिश्चिताङ्गः ॥
5.m: Having thus assumed the form of Time, the three-eyed one struck the Sacrifice in anger as the king of deer; / and pierced, devoid of consciousness from pain, it stood in the sky, its body studded with stars.

5.s:
nārada uvāca /
rāśayo gaditā brahmaṃstvayā dvādaśa vai mama /
teṣāṃ viśeṣato brūhi lakṣaṇāni svarūpataḥ //
5.d:
नारद उवाच ।
राशयो गदिता ब्रह्मंस्त्वया द्वादश वै मम ।
तेषां विशेषतो ब्रूहि लक्षणानि स्वरूपतः ॥
5.m: Nārada said: / 'The twelve signs have indeed been related to me by you, O Brahmin; / tell me in detail their distinguishing characteristics according to their true nature.'

5.s:
pulastya uvāca /
svarūpaṃ tava vakṣyāmi rāśīnāṃ śṛṇu nārada /
yādṛśā yatra saṃcārā yasmin sthāne vasanti ca //
5.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
स्वरूपं तव वक्ष्यामि राशीनां शृणु नारद ।
यादृशा यत्र संचारा यस्मिन् स्थाने वसन्ति च ॥
5.m: Pulastya said: / 'I shall describe to you the true nature of the signs; listen, Nārada, / what they are like, where they move, and in what place they dwell.

5.s:
meṣaḥ samānamūrtiśca ajāvikadhanādiṣu /
saṃcārasthānamevāsya dhānyaratnākarādiṣu //
5.d:
मेषः समानमूर्तिश्च अजाविकधनादिषु ।
संचारस्थानमेवास्य धान्यरत्नाकरादिषु ॥
5.m: Aries has the form of a ram, among goats, sheep, wealth, and the like; / its place of roaming is in mines of grain, jewels, and so forth,

5.s:
navaśādūlasaṃchannavasudhāyāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ /
nityaṃ carati phulleṣu sarasāṃ pulineṣu ca //
5.d:
नवशादूलसंछन्नवसुधायां च सर्वशः ।
नित्यं चरति फुल्लेषु सरसां पुलिनेषु च ॥
5.m: and all over the earth covered with fresh green grass; / it always moves among flowering [plants] and on the sandy banks of lakes.

5.s:
vṛṣaḥ sadṛśarūpo hi carate gokulādiṣu /
tasyādhivāsabhūmittu kuṣīvaladharāśrayaḥ //
5.d:
वृषः सदृशरूपो हि चरते गोकुलादिषु ।
तस्याधिवासभूमित्तु कुषीवलधराश्रयः ॥
5.m: Taurus, having the form of a bull, roams among cow-pens and the like; / its dwelling place is resort to the land of cultivators.

5.s:
strīpuṃsayoḥ samaṃ rūpaṃ śayyāsanaparigrahaḥ /
vīṇāvādyadhṛṅ mithunaṃ gītanartakaśilpiṣu //
5.d:
स्त्रीपुंसयोः समं रूपं शय्यासनपरिग्रहः ।
वीणावाद्यधृङ् मिथुनं गीतनर्तकशिल्पिषु ॥
5.m: The form resembles a woman and a man, taking to a bed or seat, / holding a vīṇā and musical instruments, Gemini, among singers, dancers, and artisans.

5.s:
sthitaḥ krīḍāratirnityaṃ vihārāvanirasya tu /
mithunaṃ nāma vikhyātaṃ rāśirdvedhātmakaḥ sthitaḥ //
5.d:
स्थितः क्रीडारतिर्नित्यं विहारावनिरस्य तु ।
मिथुनं नाम विख्यातं राशिर्द्वेधात्मकः स्थितः ॥
5.m: Remaining always fond of play, its ground is a pleasure-grove; / renowned by the name Gemini, the sign stands of dual nature.

5.s:
karkiḥ kulīreṇa samaḥ salilasthaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
kedāravāpīpuline viviktāvanireva ca //
5.d:
कर्किः कुलीरेण समः सलिलस्थः प्रकीर्तितः ।
केदारवापीपुलिने विविक्तावनिरेव च ॥
5.m: Cancer is like a crab, proclaimed to dwell in water, / in fields, pools, on sandbanks, and on solitary land.

5.s:
sihastu parvatāraṇyadurgakandarabhūmiṣu /
vasate vyādhapallīṣu gahvareṣu guhāsu ca //
5.d:
सिहस्तु पर्वतारण्यदुर्गकन्दरभूमिषु ।
वसते व्याधपल्लीषु गह्वरेषु गुहासु च ॥
5.m: Leo dwells in mountains, forests, forts, and cavern-lands, / in hunters' villages, in chasms, and in caves.

5.s:
vrīhipradīpikakarā manāvārūḍhā ca kanyakā /
carate strīratisthāne vasate naḍvaleṣu ca //
5.d:
व्रीहिप्रदीपिककरा मनावारूढा च कन्यका ।
चरते स्त्रीरतिस्थाने वसते नड्वलेषु च ॥
5.m: Virgo is a maiden with a lamp of rice in her hand, seated in a boat; / she moves in places of women's pleasure and dwells in reed-beds.

5.s:
tulāpāṇiśca puruṣo vīthyāpaṇavicārakaḥ /
nagarādhvānaśālāsu vasate tatra nārada //
5.d:
तुलापाणिश्च पुरुषो वीथ्यापणविचारकः ।
नगराध्वानशालासु वसते तत्र नारद ॥
5.m: Libra is a man holding a balance in his hand, inspecting streets and markets; / he dwells there, O Nārada, in cities, roads, and market-stalls.

5.s:
śvabhravalmīkasaṃcārī vṛściko vṛścikākṛtiḥ /
viṣagomayakīṭādipāṣāṇādiṣu saṃsthitaḥ //
5.d:
श्वभ्रवल्मीकसंचारी वृश्चिको वृश्चिकाकृतिः ।
विषगोमयकीटादिपाषाणादिषु संस्थितः ॥
5.m: Scorpio moves in pits and ant-hills, having the form of a scorpion; / it abides in poison, cow-dung, insects, stones, and the like.

5.s:
dhanustu raṅgajaghano dīpyamāno dhanurdharaḥ /
vājiśūrāstravidvīraḥ sthāyī gajarathādiṣu //
5.d:
धनुस्तु रङ्गजघनो दीप्यमानो धनुर्धरः ।
वाजिशूरास्त्रविद्वीरः स्थायी गजरथादिषु ॥
5.m: Sagittarius has the hips of a horse, shining, holding a bow; / a hero skilled in horses, valour, and weapons, abiding in elephants, chariots, and the like.

5.s:
mṛgāsyo makaro brahman vṛṣaskandhekṣaṇāṅgajaḥ /
makaro 'sau nadīcārī vasate ca mahodadhau //
5.d:
मृगास्यो मकरो ब्रह्मन् वृषस्कन्धेक्षणाङ्गजः ।
मकरो ऽसौ नदीचारी वसते च महोदधौ ॥
5.m: Capricorn has the face of a deer, O Brahmin, with the shoulders and eyes of a bull; / this makara moves in rivers and dwells in the great ocean.

5.s:
riktamumbhaśca puruṣaḥ skandhadhārī jalāplutaḥ /
dyūtaśālācaraḥ kumbhaḥ sthāyī śauṇḍikasadmasu //
5.d:
रिक्तमुम्भश्च पुरुषः स्कन्धधारी जलाप्लुतः ।
द्यूतशालाचरः कुम्भः स्थायी शौण्डिकसद्मसु ॥
5.m: Aquarius is a man with an empty pot, carrying it on his shoulder, bathed in water; / moving in gambling-houses, Aquarius abides in the dwellings of liquor-sellers.

5.s:
mīnadvayamathāsaktaṃ mīnastīrthābdhisaṃcaraḥ /
vasate puṇyadeśeṣu devabrāhnaṇasadmasu //
5.d:
मीनद्वयमथासक्तं मीनस्तीर्थाब्धिसंचरः ।
वसते पुण्यदेशेषु देवब्राह्नणसद्मसु ॥
5.m: Then Pisces is a pair of fish clinging together; Pisces moves in sacred waters and the sea; / it dwells in holy regions and in the abodes of gods and Brahmins.

5.s:
lakṣaṇā gaditāstubhyaṃ meṣādīnāṃ mahāmune /
na kasyacit tvayākhyeyaṃ guhyametatpurātanam //
5.d:
लक्षणा गदितास्तुभ्यं मेषादीनां महामुने ।
न कस्यचित् त्वयाख्येयं गुह्यमेतत्पुरातनम् ॥
5.m: The characteristics of Aries and the others have been told to you, O great sage; / you must not disclose this ancient secret to anyone.

5.s:
etan mayā te kathitaṃ surarṣe yathā trinetraḥ pramātha yajñam /
puṇyaṃ purāṇaṃ paramaṃ pavitramākhyātavānpāpaharaṃ śivaṃ ca //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ
5.d:
एतन् मया ते कथितं सुरर्षे यथा त्रिनेत्रः प्रमाथ यज्ञम् ।
पुण्यं पुराणं परमं पवित्रमाख्यातवान्पापहरं शिवं च ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे पञ्चमो ऽध्यायः
5.m:
This has been told to you by me, O celestial sage, how the three-eyed one destroyed the sacrifice; / I have recounted the holy, supreme, pure, sin-removing, and auspicious Purāṇa.'

Thus ends the fifth chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

6.s:
pulastya uvāca /
hṛdbhavo brahmaṇo yo 'sau dharmo divyavapurmune /
dākṣāyāṇī tasya bhāryā tasyāmajanayatsutān //
6.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
हृद्भवो ब्रह्मणो यो ऽसौ धर्मो दिव्यवपुर्मुने ।
दाक्षायाणी तस्य भार्या तस्यामजनयत्सुतान् ॥
6.m: Pulastya said: / 'Dharma, who was born from the heart of Brahmā, having a divine body, O sage, / had Dākṣāyaṇī as his wife; upon her he begot sons:

6.s:
hariṃ kuṣṇaṃ ca devarṣe nārāyaṇanarau tathā /
yogābhyāsaratau nityaṃ harikṛṣṇau babhūvatuḥ //
6.d:
हरिं कुष्णं च देवर्षे नारायणनरौ तथा ।
योगाभ्यासरतौ नित्यं हरिकृष्णौ बभूवतुः ॥
6.m: Hari and Kṛṣṇa, O celestial sage, as well as Nārāyaṇa and Nara; / Hari and Kṛṣṇa were constantly engaged in the practice of yoga,

6.s:
naranārāyaṇau caiva jagato hitakāmyayā /
tapyetāṃ ca tapaḥ saumyau purāṇavṛṣisattmau //
6.d:
नरनारायणौ चैव जगतो हितकाम्यया ।
तप्येतां च तपः सौम्यौ पुराणवृषिसत्त्मौ ॥
6.m: and Nara and Nārāyaṇa, desiring the welfare of the world, / the two gentle, foremost ancient sages, performed austerities.

6.s:
prāleyādriṃ samāgamya tīrthe badarikāśrame /
gṛmantau tatparaṃ brahma gaṅgāyā vipule taṭe //
6.d:
प्रालेयाद्रिं समागम्य तीर्थे बदरिकाश्रमे ।
गृमन्तौ तत्परं ब्रह्म गङ्गाया विपुले तटे ॥
6.m: Having come to the Snowy Mountain at the holy site of Badarikāśrama, / chanting that Supreme Brahman on the broad bank of the Gaṅgā.

6.s:
naranārāyaṇābhyāṃ ca jagadetaccarācaram /
tāpitaṃ tapasā brahman śakraḥ kṣobhaṃ tadā yayau //
6.d:
नरनारायणाभ्यां च जगदेतच्चराचरम् ।
तापितं तपसा ब्रह्मन् शक्रः क्षोभं तदा ययौ ॥
6.m: By Nara and Nārāyaṇa this world of moving and unmoving beings / was heated with austerity, O Brahmin; then Śakra fell into agitation.

6.s:
saṃkṣubdhastapasā tābhyāṃ kṣobhamaṇāya śatakratuḥ /
rambhādyāpsarasaḥ śreṣṭhāḥ preṣayatsa mahāśramam //
6.d:
संक्षुब्धस्तपसा ताभ्यां क्षोभमणाय शतक्रतुः ।
रम्भाद्याप्सरसः श्रेष्ठाः प्रेषयत्स महाश्रमम् ॥
6.m: Agitated by the austerity of those two, in order to perturb them, Śatakratu / sent the foremost apsarases, Rambhā and the others, to the great hermitage.

6.s:
kandarpaśca sudurdharṣaścūtāṅkuramahāyudhaḥ /
samaṃ sahacareṇaiva vasantenāśramaṃ gataḥ //
6.d:
कन्दर्पश्च सुदुर्धर्षश्चूताङ्कुरमहायुधः ।
समं सहचरेणैव वसन्तेनाश्रमं गतः ॥
6.m: And Kandarpa, difficult to overcome, having the sprout of a mango tree as his great weapon, / went to the hermitage together with his companion Spring.

6.s:
tato mādhavakandarpau tāścaivāpsaraso varāḥ /
badaryāśramamāgamya vicikrīḍuryathecchayā //
6.d:
ततो माधवकन्दर्पौ ताश्चैवाप्सरसो वराः ।
बदर्याश्रममागम्य विचिक्रीडुर्यथेच्छया ॥
6.m: Then Spring and Kandarpa, and those excellent apsarases, / having reached Badaryāśrama, sported as they wished.

6.s:
tato vasante saṃprāpte siṃśukā jvalanaprabhāḥ /
niṣpatrāḥ satataṃ rejuḥ śomabhayanto dharātalam //
6.d:
ततो वसन्ते संप्राप्ते सिंशुका ज्वलनप्रभाः ।
निष्पत्राः सततं रेजुः शोमभयन्तो धरातलम् ॥
6.m: Then, when Spring had arrived, the kiṃśuka trees, glowing like fire, / constantly shone without leaves, adorning the surface of the earth.

6.s:
śiśiraṃ nāma mātaṅgaṃ vidārya nakharairiva /
vasantakesarī prāptaḥ palāśakusumairmune //
6.d:
शिशिरं नाम मातङ्गं विदार्य नखरैरिव ।
वसन्तकेसरी प्राप्तः पलाशकुसुमैर्मुने ॥
6.m: As if tearing the elephant named Winter with its claws, / the lion of Spring arrived with flowers of palāśa, O sage.

6.s:
mayā tuṣāraughakarī nirjitaḥ svena tejasā /
tameva hasatetyuccaiḥ vasantaḥ kundakuḍmalaiḥ //
6.d:
मया तुषारौघकरी निर्जितः स्वेन तेजसा ।
तमेव हसतेत्युच्चैः वसन्तः कुन्दकुड्मलैः ॥
6.m: "The elephant of the mass of frost was conquered by me through my own splendour"— / thus Spring laughed aloud, as it were, with jasmine buds.

6.s:
vanāni karṇikārāṇāṃ puṣpitāni virejire /
yathā narendraputrāṇi kanakābharaṇāni hi //
6.d:
वनानि कर्णिकाराणां पुष्पितानि विरेजिरे ।
यथा नरेन्द्रपुत्राणि कनकाभरणानि हि ॥
6.m: The groves of karṇikāra trees in full bloom shone resplendent, / like the sons of kings adorned with gold ornaments.'

6.s:
teṣāmanu tathā nīpāḥ piṅkarā iva rejire /
svamisaṃlabdhasaṃmānā bhṛtyā rājasutāniva //
6.d:
तेषामनु तथा नीपाः पिङ्करा इव रेजिरे ।
स्वमिसंलब्धसंमाना भृत्या राजसुतानिव ॥
6.m: Following them, the kadamba trees shone like attendants / who had received honors from their master, like servants attending princes.

6.s:
raktāśokavanā bhānti puṣpitāḥ sahasojjvalāḥ /
bhṛtvā vasantanṛpateḥ saṃgrāme 'sṛkplutā iva //
6.d:
रक्ताशोकवना भान्ति पुष्पिताः सहसोज्ज्वलाः ।
भृत्वा वसन्तनृपतेः संग्रामे ऽसृक्प्लुता इव ॥
6.m: Groves of red aśokas shone, flowering and suddenly blazing, / like servants of King Spring bathed in blood upon a battlefield.

6.s:
mṛgavṛndāḥ piñjaritā rājante gahane vane /
pulakābhirvṛtā yadvat sajjanāḥ suhṛdāgame //
6.d:
मृगवृन्दाः पिञ्जरिता राजन्ते गहने वने ।
पुलकाभिर्वृता यद्वत् सज्जनाः सुहृदागमे ॥
6.m: Flocks of deer, dappled tawny, shone in the dense forest, / like good men filled with horripilation when a friend arrives.

6.s:
mañjarībhirvirājante nadīkūleṣu vetasāḥ /
vaktukāmā ivāṅgulyā ko 'smākaṃ sadṛśo nagaḥ //
6.d:
मञ्जरीभिर्विराजन्ते नदीकूलेषु वेतसाः ।
वक्तुकामा इवाङ्गुल्या को ऽस्माकं सदृशो नगः ॥
6.m: The reeds shone on the riverbanks with their flower-spikes, / as if wishing to say with a raised finger: 'What tree is equal to us?'

6.s:
raktāśokakarā tanvī devarṣe kiśukāṅghrikā /
nīlāśokakacā śyāmā vikāsikamalānanā //
6.d:
रक्ताशोककरा तन्वी देवर्षे किशुकाङ्घ्रिका ।
नीलाशोककचा श्यामा विकासिकमलानना ॥
6.m: Slender, with red aśoka flowers for hands, O divine sage, and kiṃśukas for feet, / with black aśokas for hair, dark, her face an opening lotus,

6.s:
nīlendīvaranetrā ca brahman bilvaphalastanī /
praphullakundadaśanā mañjarīkaraśobhitā //
6.d:
नीलेन्दीवरनेत्रा च ब्रह्मन् बिल्वफलस्तनी ।
प्रफुल्लकुन्ददशना मञ्जरीकरशोभिता ॥
6.m: her eyes blue lotuses, O Brahmin, her breasts bilva fruits, / her teeth blooming kunda flowers, adorned with flower-spikes for hands,

6.s:
bandhujīvādharā śubhrā sinduvāranakhādbhatā /
puṃskokilasvanā divyā aṅkolavasanā śubhā //
6.d:
बन्धुजीवाधरा शुभ्रा सिन्दुवारनखाद्भता ।
पुंस्कोकिलस्वना दिव्या अङ्कोलवसना शुभा ॥
6.m: her lower lip a bandhujīva flower, radiant, her nails wondrous sinduvāra buds, / her voice that of male cuckoos, divine, beautifully robed in aṅkola trees,

6.s:
barhivṛndakalāpā ca sārasasvaranūpurā /
prāgvaṃśarasanā brahman mattahaṃsagatistathā //
6.d:
बर्हिवृन्दकलापा च सारसस्वरनूपुरा ।
प्राग्वंशरसना ब्रह्मन् मत्तहंसगतिस्तथा ॥
6.m: the plumage of peacocks her trailing ornaments, the cry of cranes her anklets, / the prāgvaṃśa grass her girdle, O Brahmin, moving like an intoxicated goose,

6.s:
putrajīvāṃśukā bhṛṅgaromarājivirājitā /
vasantalakṣmīḥ saṃprāptā ba3hman badarikāśrame //
6.d:
पुत्रजीवांशुका भृङ्गरोमराजिविराजिता ।
वसन्तलक्ष्मीः संप्राप्ता ब3ह्मन् बदरिकाश्रमे ॥
6.m: clad in putrajīva leaves, adorned with lines of hair like black bees— / the Goddess of Spring thus arrived, O Brahmin, at Badarikāśrama.

6.s:
tato nārāyaṇo dṛṣṭvā āśramasyānavadyatām /
samīkṣya ca diśaḥ sarvāstato 'naṅgamapaśyata //
6.d:
ततो नारायणो दृष्ट्वा आश्रमस्यानवद्यताम् ।
समीक्ष्य च दिशः सर्वास्ततो ऽनङ्गमपश्यत ॥
6.m: Then Nārāyaṇa, seeing the faultlessness of the hermitage / and scanning all the quarters, beheld Ananga there.

6.s:
nārada uvāca/ /
ko 'sāvanaṅgo brahmarṣe tasmin badarikāśrame /
yaṃ dadarśa jagannātho devo nārāyaṇo 'vyayaḥ //
6.d:
नारद उवाच। ।
को ऽसावनङ्गो ब्रह्मर्षे तस्मिन् बदरिकाश्रमे ।
यं ददर्श जगन्नाथो देवो नारायणो ऽव्ययः ॥
6.m: Nārada said: / Who was that Ananga, O Brahmin sage, at that Badarikāśrama, / whom the Lord of the universe, the imperishable god Nārāyaṇa, saw?

6.s:
pulastya uvāca /
kandarpo harṣatanayo yo 'sau kāmo nigadyate /
sa śaṅkareṇa saṃdagdho hyanaṅgatvamupāgataḥ //
6.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
कन्दर्पो हर्षतनयो यो ऽसौ कामो निगद्यते ।
स शङ्करेण संदग्धो ह्यनङ्गत्वमुपागतः ॥
6.m: Pulastya said: / Kandarpa, the son of Joy, who is called Kāma— / burnt by Śaṅkara, he attained the state of being bodiless.

6.s:
nārada uvāca /
kimarthaṃ kāmadevo 'sau devadevena śaṃbhunā /
dagdhastu kāraṇe kasminnetadvyākhyātumarhasi //
6.d:
नारद उवाच ।
किमर्थं कामदेवो ऽसौ देवदेवेन शंभुना ।
दग्धस्तु कारणे कस्मिन्नेतद्व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
6.m: Nārada said: / Why was that god Kāmadeva burnt by Śambhu, the god of gods? / For what reason? You ought to explain this.

6.s:
pulastya uvāca /
yadā dakṣasutā brahman satī yātā yamakṣayam /
vināśya dakṣayajñaṃ taṃ vicacāra trilocanaḥ //
6.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
यदा दक्षसुता ब्रह्मन् सती याता यमक्षयम् ।
विनाश्य दक्षयज्ञं तं विचचार त्रिलोचनः ॥
6.m: Pulastya said: / When Dakṣa's daughter Satī went to the abode of Yama, O Brahmin, / the three-eyed god, having destroyed that sacrifice of Dakṣa, wandered about.

6.s:
tato vṛṣadhvajaṃ dṛṣṭvā kandarpaḥ kusumāyudhaḥ /
apatnīkaṃ tadāstreṇa unmādenābhyatāḍayat //
6.d:
ततो वृषध्वजं दृष्ट्वा कन्दर्पः कुसुमायुधः ।
अपत्नीकं तदास्त्रेण उन्मादेनाभ्यताडयत् ॥
6.m: Then Kandarpa, whose weapons are flowers, seeing the bull-bannered god / bereft of his wife, struck him with the weapon of madness.

6.s:
tato haraḥ śareṇātha unmādenāśu tāḍitaḥ /
vicacāra tadonmattaḥ kānanāni sarāṃsi ca //
6.d:
ततो हरः शरेणाथ उन्मादेनाशु ताडितः ।
विचचार तदोन्मत्तः काननानि सरांसि च ॥
6.m: Then Hara, swiftly struck by that arrow of madness, / wandered mad through forests and lakes.

6.s:
smaran satīṃ mahādevastathonmādena tāḍitaḥ /
na śarma lebhe devarṣe bāṇaviddha iva dvipaḥ //
6.d:
स्मरन् सतीं महादेवस्तथोन्मादेन ताडितः ।
न शर्म लेभे देवर्षे बाणविद्ध इव द्विपः ॥
6.m: Remembering Satī, Mahādeva, struck by madness, / found no peace, O divine sage, like an elephant pierced by an arrow.

6.s:
tataḥ papāta deveśaḥ kālindīsaritaṃ mune /
nimagne śaṅkare āpo dagdhāḥ kṛṣṇātvamāgatāḥ //
6.d:
ततः पपात देवेशः कालिन्दीसरितं मुने ।
निमग्ने शङ्करे आपो दग्धाः कृष्णात्वमागताः ॥
6.m: Then the lord of gods plunged into the river Kālindī, O sage; / when Śaṅkara submerged, the burnt waters turned black.

6.s:
tadāprabhṛti kālindyā bhṛṅgāñjananibhaṃ jalam /
āsyandat puṇyatīrthā sā keśapāśamivāvane //
6.d:
तदाप्रभृति कालिन्द्या भृङ्गाञ्जननिभं जलम् ।
आस्यन्दत् पुण्यतीर्था सा केशपाशमिवावने ॥
6.m: Ever since, the water of the Kālindī resembles black bees and collyrium, / flowing as a sacred tīrtha like a braid of hair on the earth.

6.s:
tato nadīṣu puṇyāsu sarassu ca nadeṣu ca /
puluneṣu ca ramyeṣu vāpīṣu nalinīṣu ca //
6.d:
ततो नदीषु पुण्यासु सरस्सु च नदेषु च ।
पुलुनेषु च रम्येषु वापीषु नलिनीषु च ॥
6.m: Then in holy rivers, in lakes and streams, / on lovely sandbanks, ponds, and lotus-pools,

6.s:
parvateṣu ca ramyeṣu kānaneṣu ca sānuṣu /
vicāran svecchayā naiva śarma lebhe maheśvaraḥ //
6.d:
पर्वतेषु च रम्येषु काननेषु च सानुषु ।
विचारन् स्वेच्छया नैव शर्म लेभे महेश्वरः ॥
6.m: on lovely mountains, in forests and on ridges, / wandering at will, Maheśvara found no peace at all.

6.s:
kṣaṇaṃ gāyati devarṣe kṣaṇaṃ roditi śaṅkaraḥ /
kṣaṇaṃ dhyāyati tanvaṅgīṃ dakṣakanyāṃ manoramām //
6.d:
क्षणं गायति देवर्षे क्षणं रोदिति शङ्करः ।
क्षणं ध्यायति तन्वङ्गीं दक्षकन्यां मनोरमाम् ॥
6.m: For a moment he sings, O divine sage, for a moment Śaṅkara weeps; / for a moment he meditates on Dakṣa's slender-limbed, charming daughter.

6.s:
dhyātvā kṣaṇaṃ prasvapiti kṣaṇaṃ svapnāyate haraḥ /
svapne tathedaṃ gadati tāṃ dṛṣṭvā dakṣakanyakām //
6.d:
ध्यात्वा क्षणं प्रस्वपिति क्षणं स्वप्नायते हरः ।
स्वप्ने तथेदं गदति तां दृष्ट्वा दक्षकन्यकाम् ॥
6.m: Having meditated for a moment, he falls asleep; for a moment Hara dreams; / in his dream, seeing that daughter of Dakṣa, he speaks thus:

6.s:
nirghṛṇe tiṣṭha kiṃ mūḍhe tyajase māmanindite /
mugdhe tvayā virahito dagdho 'smi madanāgninā //
6.d:
निर्घृणे तिष्ठ किं मूढे त्यजसे मामनिन्दिते ।
मुग्धे त्वया विरहितो दग्धो ऽस्मि मदनाग्निना ॥
6.m: 'Cruel one, stay! Why do you abandon me, O foolish one, blameless one? / O lovely one, separated from you I am burnt by the fire of love!

6.s:
sati satyaṃ prakupitā mā kopaṃ kuru sundari /
pādapraṇāmāvanatamabhibhāṣitu marhasi //
6.d:
सति सत्यं प्रकुपिता मा कोपं कुरु सुन्दरि ।
पादप्रणामावनतमभिभाषितु मर्हसि ॥
6.m: O Satī, are you truly enraged? Do not be angry, beautiful lady! / You ought to speak to me, bowed down in salutation at your feet!

6.s:
śrūyase dṛśyase nityaṃ spṛśyase vandyase priye /
āliṅgyase ca satataṃ kimarthaṃ nābhibhāṣase //
6.d:
श्रूयसे दृश्यसे नित्यं स्पृश्यसे वन्द्यसे प्रिये ।
आलिङ्ग्यसे च सततं किमर्थं नाभिभाषसे ॥
6.m: You are heard, seen, touched, and praised constantly, my beloved; / you are embraced perpetually. Why do you not speak to me?

6.s:
vilapantaṃ janaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛpā kasya na jāyate /
viśeṣataḥ patiṃ bāle nanupa tvamatinirghṛṇā //
6.d:
विलपन्तं जनं दृष्ट्वा कृपा कस्य न जायते ।
विशेषतः पतिं बाले ननुप त्वमतिनिर्घृणा ॥
6.m: Seeing someone lamenting, whose pity is not aroused— / especially for a husband, O girl? Surely you are exceedingly pitiless!

6.s:
tvayoktāni vacāṃsyevaṃ pūrvaṃ mama kṛśodari /
vinā tvayā na jīveyaṃ tadasatyaṃ tvayā kṛtam //
6.d:
त्वयोक्तानि वचांस्येवं पूर्वं मम कृशोदरि ।
विना त्वया न जीवेयं तदसत्यं त्वया कृतम् ॥
6.m: Such were the words spoken by you to me formerly, O slender-waisted lady: / "Without you I could not live." You have made that a lie!

6.s:
ehyehi kāmasaṃtaptaṃ pariṣvaja sulocane /
nānyathā naśyate tāpaḥ satyenāpi śape priye //
6.d:
एह्येहि कामसंतप्तं परिष्वज सुलोचने ।
नान्यथा नश्यते तापः सत्येनापि शपे प्रिये ॥
6.m: Come, come! Embrace one tormented by desire, O fair-eyed lady! / Otherwise this burning will not perish; I swear by truth, my beloved!'

6.s:
itthaṃ vilapya svapnānte pratibuddhastu tatkṣaṇāt /
utkūjati tathāraṇye muktakaṇṭhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ //
6.d:
इत्थं विलप्य स्वप्नान्ते प्रतिबुद्धस्तु तत्क्षणात् ।
उत्कूजति तथारण्ये मुक्तकण्ठं पुनः पुनः ॥
6.m: Having thus lamented, awaking that instant at the end of his dream, / he wailed aloud again and again in the wilderness.

6.s:
taṃ kūjamānaṃ vilapantamārāt samīkṣya pācaṃ tarasā vṛṣaketanaṃ hi /
vivyādha cāpaṃ tarasā vināmya saṃtāpanāmnā tu śareṇa bhūyaḥ //
6.d:
तं कूजमानं विलपन्तमारात् समीक्ष्य पाचं तरसा वृषकेतनं हि ।
विव्याध चापं तरसा विनाम्य संतापनाम्ना तु शरेण भूयः ॥
6.m: Seeing from near the bull-bannered god crying out and lamenting, / [Kāma] swiftly bent his bow and pierced him again with the arrow named 'Tormenter'.

6.s:
saṃtāpanāstreṇa tadā sa viddho bhūyaḥ sa saṃtaptataro babhūva /
saṃtāpayaṃścāpi jagatsamagraṃ phūtkṛtya phūtkṛtya vivāsate sma //
6.d:
संतापनास्त्रेण तदा स विद्धो भूयः स संतप्ततरो बभूव ।
संतापयंश्चापि जगत्समग्रं फूत्कृत्य फूत्कृत्य विवासते स्म ॥
6.m: Pierced then by the weapon of torment, he became still more tormented; / and burning the entire world, he exhaled with loud sighs.

6.s:
taṃ cāpi bhūyo madano jaghāna vijṛṇbhaṇāstreṇa tato vijṛmbhe /
tato bhṛśaṃ kāmaśarairvitunno vijṛmbhamāṇaḥ parito bhramaṃśca //
6.d:
तं चापि भूयो मदनो जघान विजृण्भणास्त्रेण ततो विजृम्भे ।
ततो भृशं कामशरैर्वितुन्नो विजृम्भमाणः परितो भ्रमंश्च ॥
6.m: Madana struck him again with the weapon of yawning, and thereupon he yawned; / deeply tormented by the arrows of Kāma, yawning and wandering around,

6.s:
dadarśa yakṣādhipatestanūjaṃ pāñcālikaṃ nāma jagatpradhānam /
dṛṣṭvā trinetro dhanadasya putraṃ pārśvaṃ samabhyetya vaco babhāṣe /
bhrātṛvya vakṣyasi vaco yadadya tat tvaṃ kuruṣvāmitavikramo 'si //
6.d:
ददर्श यक्षाधिपतेस्तनूजं पाञ्चालिकं नाम जगत्प्रधानम् ।
दृष्ट्वा त्रिनेत्रो धनदस्य पुत्रं पार्श्वं समभ्येत्य वचो बभाषे ।
भ्रातृव्य वक्ष्यसि वचो यदद्य तत् त्वं कुरुष्वामितविक्रमो ऽसि ॥
6.m: he saw the son of the lord of Yakṣas, named Pāñcālika, foremost in the world. / Seeing the son of the giver of wealth, the three-eyed god approached his side and spoke: / 'Nephew, whatever word I say today, do that; you are of boundless prowess!'

6.s:
pāñcālika uvāca /
yannātha māṃ vakṣyasi tatkariṣye suduṣkaraṃ yadyapi devasaṃghai /
ājñāpayasvātulavīrya śaṃbho dāso 'smi te bhaktiyutastatheśa //
6.d:
पाञ्चालिक उवाच ।
यन्नाथ मां वक्ष्यसि तत्करिष्ये सुदुष्करं यद्यपि देवसंघै ।
आज्ञापयस्वातुलवीर्य शंभो दासो ऽस्मि ते भक्तियुतस्तथेश ॥
6.m: Pāñcālika said: / 'Whatever you tell me, Lord, I will do, even if it is very difficult for the hosts of gods. / Command me, O Śambhu of matchless strength! I am your servant, devoted to you, O Lord!'

6.s:
īśvara uvāca /
nāśaṃ gatāyāṃ varadāmbikāyāṃ kāmāgninā pluṣsuvigraho 'smi /
vijṛmbhaṇonmādasarairvibhinno dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi ratiṃ sukhaṃ vā //
6.d:
ईश्वर उवाच ।
नाशं गतायां वरदाम्बिकायां कामाग्निना प्लुष्सुविग्रहो ऽस्मि ।
विजृम्भणोन्मादसरैर्विभिन्नो धृतिं न विन्दामि रतिं सुखं वा ॥
6.m: The Lord said: / 'Now that the boon-bestowing mother has perished, my body is scorched by the fire of love; / shattered by the arrows of yawning and madness, I find no resolve, no pleasure, no happiness.

6.s:
vijṛmbhaṇaṃ putra tathaiva tāpamunmādamugraṃ madanapraṇunnam /
nānyaḥ pumān dhārayituṃ hi śakto muktvā bhavantaṃ hi tataḥ pratīccha //
6.d:
विजृम्भणं पुत्र तथैव तापमुन्मादमुग्रं मदनप्रणुन्नम् ।
नान्यः पुमान् धारयितुं हि शक्तो मुक्त्वा भवन्तं हि ततः प्रतीच्छ ॥
6.m: This yawning, O son, and likewise the torment and fierce madness stirred up by Madana— / no other man is capable of bearing them except you; therefore, take them!'

6.s:
pulastya uvāca /
ityevamukto vṛṣabhadhvajena yakṣaḥ pratīcchat sa vijṛmbhaṇādīn /
toṣaṃ jagāmāśu tatastriśūlī tuṣṭastadaivaṃ vacanaṃ babhāṣe //
6.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
इत्येवमुक्तो वृषभध्वजेन यक्षः प्रतीच्छत् स विजृम्भणादीन् ।
तोषं जगामाशु ततस्त्रिशूली तुष्टस्तदैवं वचनं बभाषे ॥
6.m: Pulastya said: / Addressed thus by the bull-bannered god, the Yakṣa accepted the yawning and the rest; / then the trident-bearer swiftly attained satisfaction, and being pleased, spoke these words:

6.s:
hara uvāca /
yasmāttvayā putra sudurdharāṇi vijṛmbhaṇādīn pratīcchitāni /
tasmādvaraṃ tvāṃ pratipūjanāya dāsyāmi lokya ca hāsyakāri //
6.d:
हर उवाच ।
यस्मात्त्वया पुत्र सुदुर्धराणि विजृम्भणादीन् प्रतीच्छितानि ।
तस्माद्वरं त्वां प्रतिपूजनाय दास्यामि लोक्य च हास्यकारि ॥
6.m: Hara said: / 'Because, O son, you have accepted the yawning and other [afflictions], so hard to endure, / therefore I will grant you a boon for your worship, which will bring laughter to the world.

6.s:
yastvāṃ yadā paśyati caitramāse spṛśennaro vārcayate ca bhaktyā /
vṛddho 'tha bālo 'tha yuvātha yoṣit sarve tadonmādadharā bhavanti //
6.d:
यस्त्वां यदा पश्यति चैत्रमासे स्पृशेन्नरो वार्चयते च भक्त्या ।
वृद्धो ऽथ बालो ऽथ युवाथ योषित् सर्वे तदोन्मादधरा भवन्ति ॥
6.m: Whenever a man sees you, touches you, or worships you with devotion in the month of Caitra— / whether old, child, youth, or woman—they all shall be seized by madness.

6.s:
gāyanti nṛtyanti ramanti yakṣa vādyāni yatnādapi vādayanti /
tavāgrato hāsyavaco 'bhiraktā bhavanti te yogayutāstu te syuḥ //
6.d:
गायन्ति नृत्यन्ति रमन्ति यक्ष वाद्यानि यत्नादपि वादयन्ति ।
तवाग्रतो हास्यवचो ऽभिरक्ता भवन्ति ते योगयुतास्तु ते स्युः ॥
6.m: They shall sing, dance, and make merry, O Yakṣa, and play musical instruments with eagerness; / fond of jesting words before you, they shall become united with yoga.

6.s:
mamaiva nāmnā bhavitāsi pūjyaḥ pāñcālikeśaḥ prathitaḥ pṛthivyām /
mama prasādād varado narāṇāṃ bhaviṣyase pūjyatamo 'bhigaccha //
6.d:
ममैव नाम्ना भवितासि पूज्यः पाञ्चालिकेशः प्रथितः पृथिव्याम् ।
मम प्रसादाद् वरदो नराणां भविष्यसे पूज्यतमो ऽभिगच्छ ॥
6.m: By my own name you shall be worthy of worship, renowned on earth as Pāñcālikeśa; / by my grace you shall become the bestower of boons on men, most worthy of worship. Depart!'

6.s:
ityevamukto vibhunā sa yakṣo jagāma deśān sahasaiva sarvān /
kālañjarasyottarataḥ supuṇyo deśo himādrerapi dakṣiṇasthaḥ //
6.d:
इत्येवमुक्तो विभुना स यक्षो जगाम देशान् सहसैव सर्वान् ।
कालञ्जरस्योत्तरतः सुपुण्यो देशो हिमाद्रेरपि दक्षिणस्थः ॥
6.m: Addressed thus by the lord, that Yakṣa quickly went through all the lands / north of Kālañjara, a most sacred country, situated also to the south of the snowy mountain.

6.s:
tasmin supuṇye viṣaye niviṣṭo rudraprasādādabhipūjyate 'sau /
tasmin prayāte bhagavāṃstrinetro devo 'pi vindhyaṃ girimabhyagacchat //
6.d:
तस्मिन् सुपुण्ये विषये निविष्टो रुद्रप्रसादादभिपूज्यते ऽसौ ।
तस्मिन् प्रयाते भगवांस्त्रिनेत्रो देवो ऽपि विन्ध्यं गिरिमभ्यगच्छत् ॥
6.m: Established in that most holy region, he is worshipped by the grace of Rudra. / When he had departed, the three-eyed divine Lord also went to the Vindhya mountain.

6.s:
tatrāpi madano gatvā dadarśa vṛṣaketanam /
dṛṣṭvā praharttukāmaṃ ca tataḥ prāduvacaddharaḥ //
6.d:
तत्रापि मदनो गत्वा ददर्श वृषकेतनम् ।
दृष्ट्वा प्रहर्त्तुकामं च ततः प्रादुवचद्धरः ॥
6.m: There too Madana went and saw the bull-bannered god; / and seeing him eager to strike, Hara thereupon fled.

6.s:
tato dāruvanaṃ ghoraṃ madanābhisṛto haraḥ /
viveśa ṛṣayo yatra sapatnīkā vyavasthitāḥ //
6.d:
ततो दारुवनं घोरं मदनाभिसृतो हरः ।
विवेश ऋषयो यत्र सपत्नीका व्यवस्थिताः ॥
6.m: Then, pursued by Madana, Hara entered the dread Dāruvana forest, / where the sages dwelt accompanied by their wives.

6.s:
te cāpi ṛṣayaḥ sarve dṛṣṭvā mūrdhnā natābhavan /
tatastān prāha bhagavān bhikṣā me pratidīyatām //
6.d:
ते चापि ऋषयः सर्वे दृष्ट्वा मूर्ध्ना नताभवन् ।
ततस्तान् प्राह भगवान् भिक्षा मे प्रतिदीयताम् ॥
6.m: And seeing him, all those sages bowed their heads low. / Then the Lord said to them: "Let alms be given to me."

6.s:
tataste mauninastasthuḥ sarva eva maharṣayaḥ /
tadāśramāṇi sarvāṇi paricakrāma nāradaḥ //
6.d:
ततस्ते मौनिनस्तस्थुः सर्व एव महर्षयः ।
तदाश्रमाणि सर्वाणि परिचक्राम नारदः ॥
6.m: Then all those great sages remained silent; / and he roamed through all the hermitages, O Nārada.

6.s:
taṃ praviṣṭaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā bhārgavātreyayoṣitaḥ /
prakṣobhamagaman sarvā hīnasattvāḥ samantataḥ //
6.d:
तं प्रविष्टं तदा दृष्ट्वा भार्गवात्रेययोषितः ।
प्रक्षोभमगमन् सर्वा हीनसत्त्वाः समन्ततः ॥
6.m: Seeing him entered then, the women of the Bhārgavas and Ātreyas / all fell into agitation on every side, being weak of resolve,

6.s:
ṛte tvarundhatīmekāmanasūyāṃ ca bhāminīm /
etābhyāṃ bhartṛpūjāsu taccintāsu sthitaṃ manaḥ //
6.d:
ऋते त्वरुन्धतीमेकामनसूयां च भामिनीम् ।
एताभ्यां भर्तृपूजासु तच्चिन्तासु स्थितं मनः ॥
6.m: excepting only Arundhatī and the passionate Anasūyā; / the minds of these two remained fixed on worship of their husbands and on thoughts of them.

6.s:
tataḥ saṃkṣubhitāḥ sarvā yatra yāti maheśvaraḥ /
tatra prayānti kāmārttā madavihvalitendriyāḥ //
6.d:
ततः संक्षुभिताः सर्वा यत्र याति महेश्वरः ।
तत्र प्रयान्ति कामार्त्ता मदविह्वलितेन्द्रियाः ॥
6.m: Then, utterly agitated, wherever Maheśvara went, / there they followed, afflicted by desire, their senses perturbed by passion.

6.s:
tyaktvāśramaṇi śūnyāni svānitā muniyoṣitaḥ /
anuḍajagmuryathā mattaṃ kariṇya iva kuñjaram //
6.d:
त्यक्त्वाश्रमणि शून्यानि स्वानिता मुनियोषितः ।
अनुडजग्मुर्यथा मत्तं करिण्य इव कुञ्जरम् ॥
6.m: Abandoning their own hermitages deserted, those wives of the sages / followed him like intoxicated cow-elephants following a bull in rut.

6.s:
tatastu ṛṣayo dṛṣṭvā bhārgavāṅgiraso mune /
krodhānvitābruvansarve liṅge 'sya patatāṃ bhuvi //
6.d:
ततस्तु ऋषयो दृष्ट्वा भार्गवाङ्गिरसो मुने ।
क्रोधान्विताब्रुवन्सर्वे लिङ्गे ऽस्य पततां भुवि ॥
6.m: Then, seeing this, the Bhārgava and Āṅgirasa sages, O sage, / filled with rage, all said: "May his liṅga fall to the earth!"

6.s:
tataḥ papāta devasya liṅgaṃ pṛthvīṃ vidārayan /
antarddhānaṃ jagāmātha triśūlī nīlalohitaḥ //
6.d:
ततः पपात देवस्य लिङ्गं पृथ्वीं विदारयन् ।
अन्तर्द्धानं जगामाथ त्रिशूली नीललोहितः ॥
6.m: Then the liṅga of the god fell, cleaving the earth, / and then the trident-bearing Nīlalohita vanished from sight.

6.s:
tataḥ sa patito liṅgo vibhidya vasudhātalam /
rasātalaṃ viveśāśu brahmaṇḍaṃ cordhvato 'bhinat //
6.d:
ततः स पतितो लिङ्गो विभिद्य वसुधातलम् ।
रसातलं विवेशाशु ब्रह्मण्डं चोर्ध्वतो ऽभिनत् ॥
6.m: Then that fallen liṅga, splitting the surface of the earth, / swiftly entered Rasātala, and burst through the cosmic egg above.

6.s:
tataścacāla pṛthivī girayaḥ sarito nagāḥ /
pātālabhuvanāḥ sarve jaṅgamājaṅgamairvṛtāḥ //
6.d:
ततश्चचाल पृथिवी गिरयः सरितो नगाः ।
पातालभुवनाः सर्वे जङ्गमाजङ्गमैर्वृताः ॥
6.m: Then the earth trembled, the mountains, rivers, and trees, / and all the worlds of Pātāla filled with moving and unmoving beings.

6.s:
saṃkṣubdhān bhuvanān dṛṣṭvā bhūrlokādīn pitāmahaḥ /
jagāma mādhavaṃ draṣṭuṃ kṣīrodaṃ nāma sāgaram //
6.d:
संक्षुब्धान् भुवनान् दृष्ट्वा भूर्लोकादीन् पितामहः ।
जगाम माधवं द्रष्टुं क्षीरोदं नाम सागरम् ॥
6.m: Seeing the worlds beginning with Bhūrloka agitated, the Grandfather [Brahmā] / went to see Mādhava at the ocean called Kṣīroda.

6.s:
tatra dṛṣṭvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ praṇipatya ca bhaktitaḥ /
uvāca deva bhuvanāḥ kimartha kṣubhitā vibho //
6.d:
तत्र दृष्ट्वा हृषीकेशं प्रणिपत्य च भक्तितः ।
उवाच देव भुवनाः किमर्थ क्षुभिता विभो ॥
6.m: Having seen Hṛṣīkeśa there and bowed down in devotion, / he said: "O god, why are the worlds shaken, O Lord?"

6.s:
athovāca harirbrahman śārvo liṅgo maharṣibhiḥ /
pātitastasya bhārārtā saṃcacāla vasuṃdharā //
6.d:
अथोवाच हरिर्ब्रह्मन् शार्वो लिङ्गो महर्षिभिः ।
पातितस्तस्य भारार्ता संचचाल वसुंधरा ॥
6.m: Then Hari said: "O Brahman, the liṅga of Śarva / has been felled by the great sages; afflicted by its weight, the earth trembles.

6.s:
tatastadadbhutatamaṃ śrutvā devaḥ vitāmahaḥ /
tatra gacchāma deveśa evamāha punaḥ punaḥ //
6.d:
ततस्तदद्भुततमं श्रुत्वा देवः वितामहः ।
तत्र गच्छाम देवेश एवमाह पुनः पुनः ॥
6.m: Then, having heard that most marvelous thing, the divine Grandfather / said again and again: 'Let us go there, O Lord of gods!'

6.s:
tataḥ pitāmaho devaḥ keśavaśca jagatpatiḥ /
ājagmatustamuddeśaṃ yatra liṅgaṃ bhavasya tat //
6.d:
ततः पितामहो देवः केशवश्च जगत्पतिः ।
आजग्मतुस्तमुद्देशं यत्र लिङ्गं भवस्य तत् ॥
6.m: Then the divine Grandfather and Keśava, the lord of the universe, / went to that spot where the liṅga of Bhava was.

6.s:
tato 'nantaṃ harirliṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvāruhya khageśvaram /
pātālaṃ praviveśātha vismayāntarito vibhuḥ //
6.d:
ततो ऽनन्तं हरिर्लिङ्गं दृष्ट्वारुह्य खगेश्वरम् ।
पातालं प्रविवेशाथ विस्मयान्तरितो विभुः ॥
6.m: Then Hari, seeing that infinite liṅga, mounted the lord of birds / and entered Pātāla, the Lord being filled with wonder.

6.s:
brahma padmavimānena urdhvamākramya sarvataḥ /
naivāntamalabhad brahman vismitaḥ punarāgataḥ //
6.d:
ब्रह्म पद्मविमानेन उर्ध्वमाक्रम्य सर्वतः ।
नैवान्तमलभद् ब्रह्मन् विस्मितः पुनरागतः ॥
6.m: Brahmā, traversing upwards everywhere with his lotus-aerial chariot, / found no end at all, O Brahmin; astonished, he returned.

6.s:
viṣṇurgatvātha pātālān sapta lokaparāyaṇaḥ /
cakrapāṇirviniṣkrānto lebhe 'ntaṃ na mahāmune //
6.d:
विष्णुर्गत्वाथ पातालान् सप्त लोकपरायणः ।
चक्रपाणिर्विनिष्क्रान्तो लेभे ऽन्तं न महामुने ॥
6.m: Viṣṇu, having gone to the seven Pātālas, the refuge of the worlds, / came out, holding the discus in hand, having found no end, O great sage.

6.s:
viṣṇuḥ pitāmahaścobhau haraliṅgaṃ sametya hi /
kṛtāñjalipuṭau bhūtvā stotuṃ devaṃ pracakratuḥ //
6.d:
विष्णुः पितामहश्चोभौ हरलिङ्गं समेत्य हि ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटौ भूत्वा स्तोतुं देवं प्रचक्रतुः ॥
6.m: Both Viṣṇu and the Grandfather, approaching the liṅga of Hara, / folded their hands in supplication and began to praise the god.

6.s:
haribrahmāṇāvūcatuḥ /
namo 'stu te śūlapāṇe namo 'stu vṛṣabhadhvaja /
jīmūtavāhana kave śarva tryambaka śaṅkara //
6.d:
हरिब्रह्माणावूचतुः ।
नमो ऽस्तु ते शूलपाणे नमो ऽस्तु वृषभध्वज ।
जीमूतवाहन कवे शर्व त्र्यम्बक शङ्कर ॥
6.m: Hari and Brahmā said: / "Homage to you, spear-bearer! Homage to you, bull-bannered one! / Jīmūtavāhana, seer, Śarva, Tryambaka, Śaṅkara!

6.s:
maheśvara maheśāna suparṇākṣa vṛṣākape /
dakṣayajñakṣayakara kālarūpa namo 'stu te //
6.d:
महेश्वर महेशान सुपर्णाक्ष वृषाकपे ।
दक्षयज्ञक्षयकर कालरूप नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
6.m: Maheśvara, Maheśāna, Suparṇākṣa, Vṛṣākapi, / destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice, embodiment of Time, homage to you!

6.s:
tvamādirasya jagatastvaṃ madhyaṃ parameśvara /
bhavānantaśca bhagavān sarvagastvaṃ namo 'stu te //
6.d:
त्वमादिरस्य जगतस्त्वं मध्यं परमेश्वर ।
भवानन्तश्च भगवान् सर्वगस्त्वं नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
6.m: You are the beginning of this universe, you are the middle, O Supreme Lord; / you are the infinite Lord, all-pervading: homage to you!"

6.s:
pulastya uvāca/ /
evaṃ saṃstūyamānastu tasmin dāruvane haraḥ /
svarūpī tāvidaṃ vākyamuvāca vadatāṃ varaḥ //
6.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच। ।
एवं संस्तूयमानस्तु तस्मिन् दारुवने हरः ।
स्वरूपी ताविदं वाक्यमुवाच वदतां वरः ॥
6.m: Pulastya said: / Being thus praised in that Dāruvana forest, Hara, / manifesting in his own form, spoke these words to the two of them, best among speakers:

6.s:
hara uvāca /
kimarthaṃ devatānāthau paribhūtakramaṃ tviha /
māṃ stuvāte bhṛśāsvasthaṃ kāmatāpitavigraham //
6.d:
हर उवाच ।
किमर्थं देवतानाथौ परिभूतक्रमं त्विह ।
मां स्तुवाते भृशास्वस्थं कामतापितविग्रहम् ॥
6.m: Hara said: / "For what reason, O two lords of deities, setting proper order aside here, / do you praise me, who am exceedingly unwell, my body tormented by desire?"

6.s:
devāvūcatuḥ / /
bhaktaḥ pātitaṃ liṅgaṃ yadetad bhuvi śaṅkara /
etat pragṛhyatāṃ bhūya ato deva stuvāvahe //
6.d:
देवावूचतुः । ।
भक्तः पातितं लिङ्गं यदेतद् भुवि शङ्कर ।
एतत् प्रगृह्यतां भूय अतो देव स्तुवावहे ॥
6.m: The two gods said: / "O Śaṅkara, this liṅga which was felled by the devotees onto the earth— / let this be taken back again; therefore, O god, we praise you."

6.s:
hara uvāca/ /
yadyarcayanti tridaśā mama liṅgaṃ surottamau /
tadetatpratigṛhṇīyāṃ nānyatheti kathañcana //
6.d:
हर उवाच। ।
यद्यर्चयन्ति त्रिदशा मम लिङ्गं सुरोत्तमौ ।
तदेतत्प्रतिगृह्णीयां नान्यथेति कथञ्चन ॥
6.m: Hara said: / "If the thirty [gods] worship my liṅga, O best of gods, / then I shall take it back, not otherwise in any way."

6.s:
tataḥ provāca bhagavānevamastviti keśava /
brahma svayaṃ ca jagrāha liṅgaṃ kanakapiṅgalam //
tataścakāra bhagavāṃścāturvarṇyaṃ harārcane /
śāstrāṇi caiṣāṃ mukhyāni nānoktividitāni ca / /
6.d:
ततः प्रोवाच भगवानेवमस्त्विति केशव ।
ब्रह्म स्वयं च जग्राह लिङ्गं कनकपिङ्गलम् ॥
ततश्चकार भगवांश्चातुर्वर्ण्यं हरार्चने ।
शास्त्राणि चैषां मुख्यानि नानोक्तिविदितानि च । ।
6.m:
Then the Lord Keśava said: "So be it!" / And Brahmā himself took up the golden-tawny liṅga.

Then the Blessed Lord instituted the four varnas in the worship of Hara,
and their principal treatises, known through various teachings.

6.s:
6.86 ādyaṃ śaivaṃ parikhyātamanyatpāśupataṃ mune /
tṛtīyaṃ kālavadanaṃ caturthaṃ ca kapālinam //
6.d:
6.86 आद्यं शैवं परिख्यातमन्यत्पाशुपतं मुने ।
तृतीयं कालवदनं चतुर्थं च कपालिनम् ॥
6.m:
The first is renowned as Śaiva, the second is Pāśupata, O sage,
the third is Kālavadana, and the fourth is Kapālin.

6.s:
śaivaścāsītsvayaṃ śaktirvasiṣṭhasya priyaḥ śrutaḥ /
tasya śiṣyo babhūvātha gopāyana iti śrutaḥ //
6.d:
शैवश्चासीत्स्वयं शक्तिर्वसिष्ठस्य प्रियः श्रुतः ।
तस्य शिष्यो बभूवाथ गोपायन इति श्रुतः ॥
6.m: The Śaiva [teacher] himself was Śakti, the beloved son of Vasiṣṭha; / his disciple then became known as Gopāyana.

6.s:
mahāpāśupataścāsīdbharadvājastapodhanaḥ /
tasya śiṣyo 'pyabhūdrājā ṛṣabhaḥ somakeśvaraḥ //
6.d:
महापाशुपतश्चासीद्भरद्वाजस्तपोधनः ।
तस्य शिष्यो ऽप्यभूद्राजा ऋषभः सोमकेश्वरः ॥
6.m: And the great Pāśupata was Bharadvāja, rich in asceticism; / his disciple was King Ṛṣabha, lord of the Somakas.

6.s:
kālasyo bhagavānāsīdāpastambastapodhanaḥ /
tasya śiṣyobhavadvaiśyo nāmnā krātheśvaro mune //
6.d:
कालस्यो भगवानासीदापस्तम्बस्तपोधनः ।
तस्य शिष्योभवद्वैश्यो नाम्ना क्राथेश्वरो मुने ॥
6.m: The venerable Āpastamba, rich in asceticism, was the Kālamukha; / his disciple, O sage, was a Vaiśya named Krātheśvara.

6.s:
mahāvratī ca dhanadastasya śiṣyaśca viryavān /
karṇodara iti khyāto jātyā śūdro mahātapāḥ //
6.d:
महाव्रती च धनदस्तस्य शिष्यश्च विर्यवान् ।
कर्णोदर इति ख्यातो जात्या शूद्रो महातपाः ॥
6.m: And the Mahāvratin was Dhanada, and his disciple was the vigorous / Karṇodara, a Śūdra by caste, of great ascetic power.

6.s:
evaṃ ma bhagavānbrahma pūjanāya śivasya tu /
kṛtvā tu cāturāśramyaṃ svameva bhavanaṃ gataḥ //
6.d:
एवं म भगवान्ब्रह्म पूजनाय शिवस्य तु ।
कृत्वा तु चातुराश्रम्यं स्वमेव भवनं गतः ॥
6.m: Having thus established the four orders for the worship of Śiva, / the Lord Brahmā went to his own abode.

6.s:
gate ba3hmaṇi śarvo 'pi upasaṃhṛtya taṃ tadā /
liṅgaṃ citravane sūkṣmaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya cacāra ha /
6.93 vicarantaṃ tadā bhūyo maheśaṃ kusumāyudhaḥ /
ārātsthitvāgrato dhanvī saṃtāpayitumudyataḥ //
6.d:
गते ब3ह्मणि शर्वो ऽपि उपसंहृत्य तं तदा ।
लिङ्गं चित्रवने सूक्ष्मं प्रतिष्ठाप्य चचार ह ।
6.93 विचरन्तं तदा भूयो महेशं कुसुमायुधः ।
आरात्स्थित्वाग्रतो धन्वी संतापयितुमुद्यतः ॥
6.m:
When Brahmā had departed, Śarva too, having withdrawn that [form] at that time,
installed a subtle liṅga in Citravana and wandered forth.

As Maheśa was wandering once more, the flower-weaponed one [Kāma],
the archer standing nearby before him, prepared to torment him.

6.s:
tatastamagrato dṛṣṭvā krodhādhmātadṛśā haraḥ /
smaramālokayāmāsa śikhāgrāccaraṇāntikam //
6.d:
ततस्तमग्रतो दृष्ट्वा क्रोधाध्मातदृशा हरः ।
स्मरमालोकयामास शिखाग्राच्चरणान्तिकम् ॥
6.m: Then, seeing him in front with eyes ablaze with anger, Hara / looked upon Smara from the tip of his hair down to his feet.

6.s:
ālokitastrinetreṇa madano dyutimānapi /
prādahyata tadā brahman pādādārabhya kakṣavat //
6.d:
आलोकितस्त्रिनेत्रेण मदनो द्युतिमानपि ।
प्रादह्यत तदा ब्रह्मन् पादादारभ्य कक्षवत् ॥
6.m: Looked upon by the three-eyed god, Madana, though radiant, / began to burn then, O Brahmin, starting from his feet, like dry brushwood.

6.s:
pradahyamānau caraṇau dṛṣṭvāsau kusumāyudhaḥ /
utsasarja dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ tajjagāmātha pañcadhā //
6.d:
प्रदह्यमानौ चरणौ दृष्ट्वासौ कुसुमायुधः ।
उत्ससर्ज धनुः श्रेष्ठं तज्जगामाथ पञ्चधा ॥
6.m: Seeing his feet burning, the flower-weaponed one / dropped his excellent bow, and it split into five parts.

6.s:
yadāsīnmuṣṭibandhaṃ tu rukmapṛṣṭhaṃ mahāprabham /
sa campakatarurjātaḥ sugandhāḍhyo guṇākṛtiḥ //
6.d:
यदासीन्मुष्टिबन्धं तु रुक्मपृष्ठं महाप्रभम् ।
स चम्पकतरुर्जातः सुगन्धाढ्यो गुणाकृतिः ॥
6.m: That which was the grip, backed with gold and of great luster, / became the campaka tree, rich in fragrance and endowed with good qualities.

6.s:
nāhasthānaṃ śubhākāraṃ yadāsīdvajrabhūṣitam /
tajjātaṃ kesarāraṇyaṃ bakulaṃ nāmato mune //
6.d:
नाहस्थानं शुभाकारं यदासीद्वज्रभूषितम् ।
तज्जातं केसरारण्यं बकुलं नामतो मुने ॥
6.m: That which was the beautiful belly of the bow, adorned with diamonds, / became a grove of kesaras known by the name bakula, O sage.

6.s:
yā ca koṭī subhā hyāsīdindranīlavibhūṣitā /
jātā sā pāṭalā ramyā bhṛṅgarājivibhūṣitā //
6.d:
या च कोटी सुभा ह्यासीदिन्द्रनीलविभूषिता ।
जाता सा पाटला रम्या भृङ्गराजिविभूषिता ॥
6.m: And that tip which was fair, adorned with sapphires, / became the charming pāṭalā, adorned with swarms of black bees.

6.s:
nāhopari tathā muṣṭau sthānaṃ śaśimaṇiprabham /
pañcagulmābhavajjātī śaśāṅkakiraṇojjvalā //
6.d:
नाहोपरि तथा मुष्टौ स्थानं शशिमणिप्रभम् ।
पञ्चगुल्माभवज्जाती शशाङ्ककिरणोज्ज्वला ॥
6.m:
And above the cord, at the fist, the spot radiant like the moon-gem
became the five-clustered jātī jasmine, bright as moonbeams, O sage.

6.s:
ūrddhva muṣṭyā adhaḥ koṭyoḥ sthānaṃ vidrumabhūṣitam /
tasmādbhupuṭā mallī saṃjātā vividhā mune //
6.d:
ऊर्द्ध्व मुष्ट्या अधः कोट्योः स्थानं विद्रुमभूषितम् ।
तस्माद्भुपुटा मल्ली संजाता विविधा मुने ॥
6.m:
Above the fist and below the two ends was the spot adorned with coral;
from that, O sage, sprang various broad-petaled mallikā jasmines.

6.s:
puṣpottamāni ramyāṇi surabhīṇi ca nārada /
jātiyuktāni devena svayamācaritāni ca //
6.d:
पुष्पोत्तमानि रम्याणि सुरभीणि च नारद ।
जातियुक्तानि देवेन स्वयमाचरितानि च ॥
6.m:
These excellent, delightful and fragrant flowers, O Nārada,
endowed with beauty, were personally utilized by the god.

6.s:
mumoca mārgaṇān bhūmyāṃ śarīre dahyati smaraḥ /
phalopagāni vṛkṣāṇi saṃbhūtāni sahasraśaḥ //
6.d:
मुमोच मार्गणान् भूम्यां शरीरे दह्यति स्मरः ।
फलोपगानि वृक्षाणि संभूतानि सहस्रशः ॥
6.m:
As his body burned, Smara dropped his arrows upon the ground;
trees bearing fruit sprang up in their thousands:

6.s:
cūtādīni sugandhīni svādūni vividhāni ca /
haraprasādājjātāni bhojyānyapi surottamaiḥ //
6.d:
चूतादीनि सुगन्धीनि स्वादूनि विविधानि च ।
हरप्रसादाज्जातानि भोज्यान्यपि सुरोत्तमैः ॥
6.m:
mango and others, fragrant, sweet, and diverse,
arose by Hara’s grace, enjoyable even for the best of the gods.

6.s:
evaṃ dagdhvā smaraṃ rudraḥ saṃyamya svatanuṃ vibhuḥ /
puṣyārthā śiśirādriṃ sa jagāma tapase 'vyayaḥ //
6.d:
एवं दग्ध्वा स्मरं रुद्रः संयम्य स्वतनुं विभुः ।
पुष्यार्था शिशिराद्रिं स जगाम तपसे ऽव्ययः ॥
6.m:
Having thus burnt Smara, Rudra, the all-pervading, imperishable lord,
controlling his own form, went to the cold mountain for asceticism, for the sake of prosperity.

6.s:
evaṃ purā devavareṇa śaṃbhunā kāmastu dagdhaḥ saśaraḥ sacāpaḥ /
tatastvanaṅgeti mahādhanurddharo devaistu gītaḥ surapūrvapūjitaḥ //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ
6.d:
एवं पुरा देववरेण शंभुना कामस्तु दग्धः सशरः सचापः ।
ततस्त्वनङ्गेति महाधनुर्द्धरो देवैस्तु गीतः सुरपूर्वपूजितः ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे षष्ठो ऽध्यायः

7.s:
pulastya uvāca /
tato 'naṅgaṃ vibhurddaṣṭvā brahman nārāyaṇo muniḥ /
prahasyaivaṃ vacaḥ prāha kandarva iha āsyatām //
7.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
ततो ऽनङ्गं विभुर्द्दष्ट्वा ब्रह्मन् नारायणो मुनिः ।
प्रहस्यैवं वचः प्राह कन्दर्व इह आस्यताम् ॥
7.m:
Pulastya said:
Then, seeing the bodiless Kāma, O Brahmin, the sage Nārāyaṇa, the powerful lord,
smiled and spoke these words: ‘Let Kandarpa sit here.’

7.s:
tadakṣubdhatvamīkṣyāsya kāmo vismayamāgataḥ /
vasanto 'pi mahācintāṃ jagāmāśu mahāmune //
7.d:
तदक्षुब्धत्वमीक्ष्यास्य कामो विस्मयमागतः ।
वसन्तो ऽपि महाचिन्तां जगामाशु महामुने ॥
7.m:
Seeing his imperturbability, Kāma was filled with wonder;
Vasanta too immediately fell into deep thought, O great sage.

7.s:
tataścāpsaraso dṛṣṭvā svāgatenābhipūjya ca /
vasantamāha bhagavānehyehi sthīyatāmiti //
7.d:
ततश्चाप्सरसो दृष्ट्वा स्वागतेनाभिपूज्य च ।
वसन्तमाह भगवानेह्येहि स्थीयतामिति ॥
7.m:
Then, seeing the apsarases and honoring them with a welcome,
the Lord said to Vasanta: ‘Come, come, be seated!’

7.s:
tato vihasya bhagavān mañjarīṃ kusumāvṛtām /
ādāya prāksuvarṇāṅgīmūrvorbālāṃ vinirmame //
7.d:
ततो विहस्य भगवान् मञ्जरीं कुसुमावृताम् ।
आदाय प्राक्सुवर्णाङ्गीमूर्वोर्बालां विनिर्ममे ॥
7.m:
Then the Lord, smiling, took a flower-laden sprout
and from his thighs fashioned a girl whose limbs were of pure gold.

7.s:
ūrūdbhavāṃ sa kandarpo dṛṣṭvā sarvāṅgasundarīm /
amanyata tadānaṅgaḥ kimiyaṃ sā priyā ratiḥ //
7.d:
ऊरूद्भवां स कन्दर्पो दृष्ट्वा सर्वाङ्गसुन्दरीम् ।
अमन्यत तदानङ्गः किमियं सा प्रिया रतिः ॥
7.m:
Seeing her who was born from the thigh, beautiful in all her limbs,
that Kandarpa, the bodiless god, thought: ‘Is this my beloved Rati?’

7.s:
tadeva vadanaṃ cāru svakṣibhrūkuṭilālakam /
sunāsāvaṃśādharoṣṭhamālokanaparāyaṇam //
7.d:
तदेव वदनं चारु स्वक्षिभ्रूकुटिलालकम् ।
सुनासावंशाधरोष्ठमालोकनपरायणम् ॥
7.m:
[There was] that same lovely face, with fair eyes and curved eyebrows, and curling tresses,
with a fine nasal bridge and lower lip, absorbed in gazing;

7.s:
tāvevāhārya viralau pīvarau magnacūcukau /
rājete 'syaḥ kucau pīnau sajjanāvi saṃhatau //
7.d:
तावेवाहार्य विरलौ पीवरौ मग्नचूचुकौ ।
राजेते ऽस्यः कुचौ पीनौ सज्जनावि संहतौ ॥
7.m:
those same two plump, close-set breasts, unyielding, close together,
with sunken nipples, shone like two virtuous people united in friendship;

7.s:
tadeva tanu cārvaṅgyā valitrayavibhūṣitam /
udaraṃ rājate ślakṣṇaṃ romāvalivibhūṣitam //
7.d:
तदेव तनु चार्वङ्ग्या वलित्रयविभूषितम् ।
उदरं राजते श्लक्ष्णं रोमावलिविभूषितम् ॥
7.m:
that same slender, smooth belly of the fair-limbed maiden shone,
adorned with three folds and decorated with a line of down;

7.s:
romāvalīca jaghanād yāntī stanataṭaṃ tviyam /
rājate bhṛṅgamāleva pulināt kamalākaram //
7.d:
रोमावलीच जघनाद् यान्ती स्तनतटं त्वियम् ।
राजते भृङ्गमालेव पुलिनात् कमलाकरम् ॥
7.m:
and this line of down going from the hips to the slope of her breasts
shone like a swarm of bees moving from a sandbank to a lotus-pool;

7.s:
jaghanaṃ tvativistīrṇa bhātyasyā raśanāvṛtam /
śrīrodamathane naddhūṃ bhūjaṅgeneva mandaram //
7.d:
जघनं त्वतिविस्तीर्ण भात्यस्या रशनावृतम् ।
श्रीरोदमथने नद्धूं भूजङ्गेनेव मन्दरम् ॥
7.m:
her broad hips, encircled by a girdle, shone
like Mount Mandara bound by the serpent during the churning of the ocean of milk;

7.s:
kadalīstambhasadṛśairūrdhvamūlairathorubhiḥ /
vibhāti sā sucārvaṅgī padmakiḍhjalkasannibhā //
7.d:
कदलीस्तम्भसदृशैरूर्ध्वमूलैरथोरुभिः ।
विभाति सा सुचार्वङ्गी पद्मकिढ्जल्कसन्निभा ॥
7.m:
with thighs like plantain trunks, tapering upwards,
that fair-limbed maiden shone, resembling the filament of a lotus;

7.s:
jānunī gūḍhagulphe ca śubhe jaṅghe tvaromaśe /
vibhāto 'syāstathā pādāvalaktakasamatviṣau //
7.d:
जानुनी गूढगुल्फे च शुभे जङ्घे त्वरोमशे ।
विभातो ऽस्यास्तथा पादावलक्तकसमत्विषौ ॥
7.m:
her knees and hidden ankles, and her lovely hairless shanks;
likewise her two feet shone, radiant as red lac.

7.s:
iti saṃcintayan kāmastāmaninditalocanām /
kāmāturo 'sau saṃjātaḥ kimutānyo jano mune //
7.d:
इति संचिन्तयन् कामस्तामनिन्दितलोचनाम् ।
कामातुरो ऽसौ संजातः किमुतान्यो जनो मुने ॥
7.m:
Thinking thus, Kāma, gazing at her with faultless eyes,
became overcome with desire—what then of any other person, O sage?

7.s:
mādhavo 'pyurvaśīṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃcintayata nārada /
kiṃsvit kāmanarendrasya rājadhānī svayaṃ sthitā //
7.d:
माधवो ऽप्युर्वशीं दृष्ट्वा संचिन्तयत नारद ।
किंस्वित् कामनरेन्द्रस्य राजधानी स्वयं स्थिता ॥
7.m:
Mādhava too, seeing Urvaśī, thought, O Nārada:
‘Could this be the personal capital city of the king of desire?

7.s:
āyātā śaśino nūnamiyaṃ kāntirniśākṣaye /
raviraśmipratāpārtibhītā śaraṇamāgatā //
7.d:
आयाता शशिनो नूनमियं कान्तिर्निशाक्षये ।
रविरश्मिप्रतापार्तिभीता शरणमागता ॥
7.m:
Surely this is the radiance of the moon come at the end of night,
frightened by the affliction of the sun’s blazing rays, seeking refuge!’

7.s:
itthaṃ saṃcitayanneva avaṣṭabhāpsarogaṇam /
tasthau muniriva dhyānamāsthitaḥ sa tu mādhavaḥ //
7.d:
इत्थं संचितयन्नेव अवष्टभाप्सरोगणम् ।
तस्थौ मुनिरिव ध्यानमास्थितः स तु माधवः ॥
7.m:
Reflecting thus and checking the host of apsarases,
that Mādhava stood firm, like an ascetic absorbed in meditation.

7.s:
tataḥ sa vismitān sarvān kandarpādīn mahāmune /
dṛṣṭvā provāca vacanaṃ smitaṃ kṛtvā śubhavrataḥ //
7.d:
ततः स विस्मितान् सर्वान् कन्दर्पादीन् महामुने ।
दृष्ट्वा प्रोवाच वचनं स्मितं कृत्वा शुभव्रतः ॥
7.m:
Then, seeing Kandarpa and the others all astonished, O great sage,
he of auspicious vows smiled and spoke these words:

7.s:
iyaṃ mamorusaṃbhṛtā kāmāpsarasa mādhava /
nīyatāṃ suralokāya dīyatāṃ vāsavāya ca //
7.d:
इयं ममोरुसंभृता कामाप्सरस माधव ।
नीयतां सुरलोकाय दीयतां वासवाय च ॥
7.m:
‘This Urvaśī, produced from my thigh, O Kāma, apsarases, and Mādhava,
let her be taken to the celestial world and given to Indra.’

7.s:
ityuktāḥ kampamānāste jagmurgṛhyorvaśīṃ divam /
sahasrākṣāya tāṃ prādād rūpayauvanaśālinīm //
7.d:
इत्युक्ताः कम्पमानास्ते जग्मुर्गृह्योर्वशीं दिवम् ।
सहस्राक्षाय तां प्रादाद् रूपयौवनशालिनीम् ॥
7.m:
Thus addressed, they, trembling, took Urvaśī and went to heaven;
they delivered her, possessing beauty and youth, to the thousand-eyed Indra.

7.s:
ācakṣuścaritaṃ tābhyāṃ dharmajābhyāṃ mahāmune /
devārājāya kāmādyāstato 'bhṛd vismayaḥ paraḥ //
7.d:
आचक्षुश्चरितं ताभ्यां धर्मजाभ्यां महामुने ।
देवाराजाय कामाद्यास्ततो ऽभृद् विस्मयः परः ॥
7.m:
Kāma and the others reported the deed of the two sons of Dharma
to the king of the gods, O great sage; then supreme wonder arose [in him].

7.s:
etādśaṃ hi caritaṃ khyātimagryāṃ jagāma ha /
pātāleṣu tathā martyai dikṣvaṣṭāsu jagāma ca //
7.d:
एताद्शं हि चरितं ख्यातिमग्र्यां जगाम ह ।
पातालेषु तथा मर्त्यै दिक्ष्वष्टासु जगाम च ॥
7.m:
Indeed, such an exploit achieved the highest renown
in the realms of Pātāla, among mortals, and across the eight directions.

7.s:
ekadā nihate raudro hiraṇyakaśipau mune /
abhiṣiktastadā rājye prahlādau nāma dānavaḥ //
7.d:
एकदा निहते रौद्रो हिरण्यकशिपौ मुने ।
अभिषिक्तस्तदा राज्ये प्रह्लादौ नाम दानवः ॥
7.m:
Once, O sage, when the terrible Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain,
the Dānava named Prahlāda was then consecrated in the kingdom.

7.s:
tasmiñśāsati daityendre devabrāhmaṇapūjake /
makhāni bhuvi rājāno yajante vidhivattadā //
7.d:
तस्मिञ्शासति दैत्येन्द्रे देवब्राह्मणपूजके ।
मखानि भुवि राजानो यजन्ते विधिवत्तदा ॥
7.m:
While that lord of the Daityas, a worshiper of gods and Brahmins, was ruling,
kings on earth duly performed sacrifices.

7.s:
brāhmaṇāśca tapo dharmaṃ tīrthayātrāśca kurvate /
vaiśyāśca paśuvṛttisthāḥ śūdrāḥ śuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ //
7.d:
ब्राह्मणाश्च तपो धर्मं तीर्थयात्राश्च कुर्वते ।
वैश्याश्च पशुवृत्तिस्थाः शूद्राः शुश्रूषणे रताः ॥
7.m:
Brahmins practiced austerities, virtue, and pilgrimages to tīrthas;
Vaiśyas engaged in cattle rearing, and Śūdras were devoted to service.

7.s:
cāturvarṇyaṃ tataḥ sve sve āśrame dharmakarmaṇi /
āvarttata tato devā vṛttyā yuktābhavān mune //
7.d:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं ततः स्वे स्वे आश्रमे धर्मकर्मणि ।
आवर्त्तत ततो देवा वृत्त्या युक्ताभवान् मुने ॥
7.m:
The four orders of society then conformed to their own proper stage of life and duty;
consequently, O sage, the gods became provided with their livelihood.

7.s:
tatastu cyavano nāma bhārgavendro mahātapāḥ /
jagāma narmadāṃ snātuṃ tīrthaṃ caivākulīśvaram //
7.d:
ततस्तु च्यवनो नाम भार्गवेन्द्रो महातपाः ।
जगाम नर्मदां स्नातुं तीर्थं चैवाकुलीश्वरम् ॥
7.m:
Then a great ascetic, the foremost of the Bhārgavas named Cyavana,
went to the Narmadā to bathe and to visit the Akulīśvara tīrtha.

7.s:
tatra dṛṣṭvā mahādevaṃ nadīṃ snātumavātarat /
avatīrṇaṃ prajagrāha nāgaḥ kekaralohitaḥ //
7.d:
तत्र दृष्ट्वा महादेवं नदीं स्नातुमवातरत् ।
अवतीर्णं प्रजग्राह नागः केकरलोहितः ॥
7.m:
Having seen Mahādeva there, he descended into the river to bathe;
as he descended, a squint-eyed, reddish serpent seized him.

7.s:
gṛhītastena nāgena sasmāra manasā harim /
saṃsmṛte puṇḍarīkākṣe nirviṣo 'bhūnmahoragaḥ //
7.d:
गृहीतस्तेन नागेन सस्मार मनसा हरिम् ।
संस्मृते पुण्डरीकाक्षे निर्विषो ऽभून्महोरगः ॥
7.m:
Seized by that serpent, he remembered Hari in his mind;
when the lotus-eyed one was remembered, the great serpent became devoid of poison.

7.s:
nītastenātiraudreṇa pannagena rasātalam /
nirviṣaścāpi tatyāja cyavanaṃ bhujagottamaḥ //
7.d:
नीतस्तेनातिरौद्रेण पन्नगेन रसातलम् ।
निर्विषश्चापि तत्याज च्यवनं भुजगोत्तमः ॥
7.m:
Taken to Rasātala by that exceedingly terrible serpent,
that foremost of serpents, now harmless, released Cyavana.

7.s:
saṃtyaktamātro nāgena cyavano bhārgavottamaḥ /
cacāra nāgakanyābhiḥ pūjyacamānaḥ samantataḥ //
7.d:
संत्यक्तमात्रो नागेन च्यवनो भार्गवोत्तमः ।
चचार नागकन्याभिः पूज्यचमानः समन्ततः ॥
7.m:
As soon as he was released by the serpent, Cyavana, the foremost Bhārgava,
wandered about, worshiped on all sides by the serpent maidens.

7.s:
vicāran praviveśātha dānavānāṃ mahat puram /
saṃpūjyamāno daityendraḥ prahlādo 'tha dadarśa tam //
7.d:
विचारन् प्रविवेशाथ दानवानां महत् पुरम् ।
संपूज्यमानो दैत्येन्द्रः प्रह्लादो ऽथ ददर्श तम् ॥
7.m:
Wandering, he then entered the great city of the Dānavas;
Prahlāda, the lord of the Daityas, then beheld him being honored.

7.s:
bhṛguputre mahātejāḥ pūjāṃ cakre yathārhataḥ /
saṃpūjitopaviṣṭaśca pṛṣṭaścāgamanaṃ prati //
7.d:
भृगुपुत्रे महातेजाः पूजां चक्रे यथार्हतः ।
संपूजितोपविष्टश्च पृष्टश्चागमनं प्रति ॥
7.m:
The majestic king duly offered worship to the son of Bhṛgu;
when he was honored and seated, he was asked about his arrival.

7.s:
sa covāca mahārāja mahātīrthaṃ mahāphalam /
snātumevāgato 'smyadya draṣṭuñcaivākulīśvaram //
7.d:
स चोवाच महाराज महातीर्थं महाफलम् ।
स्नातुमेवागतो ऽस्म्यद्य द्रष्टुञ्चैवाकुलीश्वरम् ॥
7.m:
And he said: ‘O great king, I came today to bathe
in a great tīrtha yielding great fruit, and to behold Akulīśvara.

7.s:
nadyāmevāvatīrṇo 'smi gṛhītaścāhinā balān /
samānīto 'smi pātāle dṛṣṭaścātra bhavānapi //
7.d:
नद्यामेवावतीर्णो ऽस्मि गृहीतश्चाहिना बलान् ।
समानीतो ऽस्मि पाताले दृष्टश्चात्र भवानपि ॥
7.m:
I had just stepped down into the river when I was forcefully seized by a serpent;
I was brought to Pātāla, and here I have seen you as well.’

7.s:
etacchrutvā tu vacanaṃ cyavanasya ditīśvaraḥ /
provāca dharmasaṃyuktaṃ sa vākyaṃ vākyakovidaḥ //
7.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं च्यवनस्य दितीश्वरः ।
प्रोवाच धर्मसंयुक्तं स वाक्यं वाक्यकोविदः ॥
7.m:
Hearing these words of Cyavana, the lord of the descendants of Diti,
skilled in speech, spoke these words endowed with righteousness:

7.s:
prahlāda uvāca /
bhagavan kāni tīrthāni pṛthivyāṃ kāni cāmbare /
rasātale ca kāni syuretad vaktuṃ mamārhasi //
7.d:
प्रह्लाद उवाच ।
भगवन् कानि तीर्थानि पृथिव्यां कानि चाम्बरे ।
रसातले च कानि स्युरेतद् वक्तुं ममार्हसि ॥
7.m:
Prahlāda said:
‘O venerable one, what are the tīrthas on earth, what are those in the sky,
and what might be in Rasātala? You ought to tell me this.’

7.s:
cyavana uvāca /
pṛthivyāṃ naimiṣaṃ tīrthamantarikṣe ca puṣkaram /
cakratīrthaṃ mahābāho rasātalatale viduḥ //
7.d:
च्यवन उवाच ।
पृथिव्यां नैमिषं तीर्थमन्तरिक्षे च पुष्करम् ।
चक्रतीर्थं महाबाहो रसातलतले विदुः ॥

7.s:
pulastya uvāca /
śrutvā tadbhārgavavaco daityarājo mahāmune /
nemiṣai gantukāmastu dānavānitadabravīt //
7.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
श्रुत्वा तद्भार्गववचो दैत्यराजो महामुने ।
नेमिषै गन्तुकामस्तु दानवानितदब्रवीत् ॥
7.m:
Pulastya said:
Having heard those words of the Bhārgava, O great sage, the king of the Daityas,
wishing to go to Naimiṣa, said to the Dānavas:

7.s:
prahlāda uvāca /
uttiṣṭhadhvaṃ gamiṣyāmaḥ snātuṃ tīrthaṃ hi naimiṣam /
drakṣyāmaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ pītavāsasamacyutam //
7.d:
प्रह्लाद उवाच ।
उत्तिष्ठध्वं गमिष्यामः स्नातुं तीर्थं हि नैमिषम् ।
द्रक्ष्यामः पुण्डरीकाक्षं पीतवाससमच्युतम् ॥

7.s:
pulastya uvāca /
ityuktā dānavendreṇa sarve te daityadānavāḥ /
cakrurudyogamatulaṃ nirjagmuśca rasātalāt //
7.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
इत्युक्ता दानवेन्द्रेण सर्वे ते दैत्यदानवाः ।
चक्रुरुद्योगमतुलं निर्जग्मुश्च रसातलात् ॥
7.m:
Pulastya said:
Thus addressed by the lord of the Dānavas, all those Daityas and Dānavas
made matchless preparation and departed from Rasātala.

7.s:
te samabhyetya daiteyā dānavāśca mahābalāḥ /
nemiṣāraṇyamāgatya snānaṃ cakrurmudānvitāḥ //
7.d:
ते समभ्येत्य दैतेया दानवाश्च महाबलाः ।
नेमिषारण्यमागत्य स्नानं चक्रुर्मुदान्विताः ॥
7.m: Those mighty Daityas and Dānavas assembled together, / and arriving at Nemiṣāraṇya, bathed with joyous hearts.

7.s:
tato ditīśvaraḥ śrīmān mṛgavyāṃ sa cacāra ha /
caran sarasvatīṃ puṇyāṃ dadarśa vimalodakām //
7.d:
ततो दितीश्वरः श्रीमान् मृगव्यां स चचार ह ।
चरन् सरस्वतीं पुण्यां ददर्श विमलोदकाम् ॥
7.m: Then the glorious lord of Diti roamed about on a deer hunt; / and as he wandered, he saw the holy Sarasvatī of spotless waters.

7.s:
tasyādūre mahāśākhaṃ śalavṛkṣaṃ śaraiścitam /
dadarśa bāṇānaparān mukhe lagnān parasparam //
7.d:
तस्यादूरे महाशाखं शलवृक्षं शरैश्चितम् ।
ददर्श बाणानपरान् मुखे लग्नान् परस्परम् ॥
7.m: Not far from it he saw a large-branched śāla tree covered with arrows, / and other arrows stuck together mouth to mouth.

7.s:
tatastānadbhutākārān bāṇān nāgopavītakān /
dṛṣṭvātulaṃ tadā cakre krodhaṃ daityeśvaraḥ kila //
7.d:
ततस्तानद्भुताकारान् बाणान् नागोपवीतकान् ।
दृष्ट्वातुलं तदा चक्रे क्रोधं दैत्येश्वरः किल ॥
7.m: Then, seeing those wondrously shaped arrows furnished with snake-like sacred threads, / the lord of the Daityas felt boundless rage.

7.s:
sa dadarśa tato 'dūrātkṛṣṇājinadharau munī /
samunnatajaṭābhārau tapasyāsaktamānasau //
7.d:
स ददर्श ततो ऽदूरात्कृष्णाजिनधरौ मुनी ।
समुन्नतजटाभारौ तपस्यासक्तमानसौ ॥
7.m: Thereupon he saw not far away two sages wearing black buckskin, / with raised masses of matted locks, their minds absorbed in austerity.

7.s:
tayośca pārśvayordivye dhanuṣī lakṣaṇānvite /
śārṅgamāgavaṃ caiva akṣyyau ca maheṣudhī //
7.d:
तयोश्च पार्श्वयोर्दिव्ये धनुषी लक्षणान्विते ।
शार्ङ्गमागवं चैव अक्ष्य्यौ च महेषुधी ॥
7.m: And at their sides were two divine bows possessed of auspicious marks, / the Śārṅga and the Ājagava, and two inexhaustible great quivers.

7.s:
tau dṛṣṭvāmanyata tadā dāmibikāviti dānavaḥ /
tataḥ provāca vacanaṃ tāvubhau puruṣottamau //
7.d:
तौ दृष्ट्वामन्यत तदा दामिबिकाविति दानवः ।
ततः प्रोवाच वचनं तावुभौ पुरुषोत्तमौ ॥
7.m: Seeing them, the Dānava then considered them to be hypocrites; / then he spoke words to both of those best among men:

7.s:
kiṃ bhavadbhyāṃ samāraḥdhaṃ dambhaṃ dharmavināśanam /
kva tapaḥ kva jaṭābhāraḥ kva cemau pravarāyudhau //
7.d:
किं भवद्भ्यां समारःधं दम्भं धर्मविनाशनम् ।
क्व तपः क्व जटाभारः क्व चेमौ प्रवरायुधौ ॥
7.m: “Why have you two undertaken deceit, which destroys righteousness? / Where is austerity, where the mass of matted locks, and where these excellent weapons?

7.s:
athovāca naro daityaṃ kā te cintā ditīśvara /
sāmarthye sati yaḥ kuryāt tatsaṃpadyeta tasya hi //
7.d:
अथोवाच नरो दैत्यं का ते चिन्ता दितीश्वर ।
सामर्थ्ये सति यः कुर्यात् तत्संपद्येत तस्य हि ॥
7.m: Then Nara said to the Daitya: “What is your concern, O lord of Diti's line? / When capacity exists, whatever one would do becomes accomplished for him.”

7.s:
athovāca ditīśastau kā śaktiryuvayoriha /
mayi tiṣṭhati daityendre dharmasetupravartake //
7.d:
अथोवाच दितीशस्तौ का शक्तिर्युवयोरिह ।
मयि तिष्ठति दैत्येन्द्रे धर्मसेतुप्रवर्तके ॥
7.m: Then the lord of Diti's line said to the two: “What is your power here, / while I, the Daitya lord and maintainer of the bridge of righteousness, am present?”

7.s:
narastaṃ pratyuvācātha āvābhyāṃ śaktirūrjitā /
na kaścicchaknuyād yoddhuṃ naranārāyaṇau yudhi //
7.d:
नरस्तं प्रत्युवाचाथ आवाभ्यां शक्तिरूर्जिता ।
न कश्चिच्छक्नुयाद् योद्धुं नरनारायणौ युधि ॥
7.m: Nara then answered him: “Ours is vast power; / no one can fight Nara and Nārāyaṇa in battle.”

7.s:
daityeśvarastastaḥ kruddhaḥ pratijñāmāruroha ca /
yathā kathañcijjeṣyāmi naranārāyaṇau raṇe //
7.d:
दैत्येश्वरस्तस्तः क्रुद्धः प्रतिज्ञामारुरोह च ।
यथा कथञ्चिज्जेष्यामि नरनारायणौ रणे ॥
7.m: Then the lord of the Daityas, enraged, took an oath: / “Somehow or other I will conquer Nara and Nārāyaṇa in battle!”

7.s:
ityevamuktvā vacanaṃ mahātmā ditīśvaraḥ sthāpya balaṃ vanānte /
vitatya cāpaṃ guṇamāvikṛṣya taladhvaniṃ ghorataraṃ cakāra //
7.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं महात्मा दितीश्वरः स्थाप्य बलं वनान्ते ।
वितत्य चापं गुणमाविकृष्य तलध्वनिं घोरतरं चकार ॥
7.m: Having spoken these words, the great-souled lord of Diti's line stationed his army at the edge of the forest; / drawing his bow and pulling the string, he made a most dreadful twang with his palms.

7.s:
tato narastvājagavaṃ hi cāpamānamya bāṇān subahuñśitāgrān /
mumoca tānapratimaiḥ pṛṣatkaiściccheda daityastapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ //
7.d:
ततो नरस्त्वाजगवं हि चापमानम्य बाणान् सुबहुञ्शिताग्रान् ।
मुमोच तानप्रतिमैः पृषत्कैश्चिच्छेद दैत्यस्तपनीयपुङ्खैः ॥
7.m: Then Nara bent the Ājagava bow and released / very many sharp-pointed arrows; the Daitya cut them down with matchless, gold-feathered shafts.

7.s:
chinnān samīkṣyātha naraḥ pṛṣatkān daityeśvareṇāpratimeva saṃkhye /
kruddhaḥ samānamya mahādhanustato mumoca cānyān vividhān pṛṣatkān //
7.d:
छिन्नान् समीक्ष्याथ नरः पृषत्कान् दैत्येश्वरेणाप्रतिमेव संख्ये ।
क्रुद्धः समानम्य महाधनुस्ततो मुमोच चान्यान् विविधान् पृषत्कान् ॥
7.m: Seeing his shafts severed in battle by the matchless lord of the Daityas, / Nara, enraged, bent his great bow and released other varied shafts.

7.s:
ekaṃ naro dvau ditijeśvaraśca trīn dharmasūnuścaturo ditīśaḥ /
narastu bāṇān pramumoca pañca ṣaḍ dratyanātho niśitān pṛṣatkān //
7.d:
एकं नरो द्वौ दितिजेश्वरश्च त्रीन् धर्मसूनुश्चतुरो दितीशः ।
नरस्तु बाणान् प्रमुमोच पञ्च षड् द्रत्यनाथो निशितान् पृषत्कान् ॥
7.m: Nara [discharged] one, the lord of Diti's sons two; the son of Dharma three, the lord of Diti's line four; / Nara discharged five arrows, the lord of the Daityas six sharpened shafts.

7.s:
saptarṣimukhyo dvicatuśca daityo narastu ṣaṭ trīṇi ca daityamukhye /
ṣaṭtrīṇi caikaṃ ca ditīśvareṇa muktāni bāṇāni narāya vipra //
7.d:
सप्तर्षिमुख्यो द्विचतुश्च दैत्यो नरस्तु षट् त्रीणि च दैत्यमुख्ये ।
षट्त्रीणि चैकं च दितीश्वरेण मुक्तानि बाणानि नराय विप्र ॥
7.m: The foremost of the seven sages [discharged] eight and the Daitya two fours; Nara [shot] eighteen at the Daitya chief; / and eighteen and one arrows were shot by the lord of Diti's line at Nara, O Brahmin.

7.s:
ekaṃ ca ṣaṭ pañca nareṇa muktāstvaṣṭau śarāḥ sapta ca dānavena /
ṣaṭ sapta cāṣṭau nava ṣaṇnareṇa dvisaptatiṃ daityapatiḥ sasarjja //
7.d:
एकं च षट् पञ्च नरेण मुक्तास्त्वष्टौ शराः सप्त च दानवेन ।
षट् सप्त चाष्टौ नव षण्नरेण द्विसप्ततिं दैत्यपतिः ससर्ज्ज ॥
7.m: One and six and five were shot by Nara, but eight and seven arrows by the Dānava; / six, seven, eight, nine, and six by Nara; seventy-two the lord of the Daityas discharged.

7.s:
śataṃ narastrīṇi śatāni daityaḥ ṣaḍ dharmaputro daśa daityarājaḥ /
tato 'pyasaṃkhyeyatarān hi bāṇān mumocatustau subhṛśaṃ hi kopāt //
7.d:
शतं नरस्त्रीणि शतानि दैत्यः षड् धर्मपुत्रो दश दैत्यराजः ।
ततो ऽप्यसंख्येयतरान् हि बाणान् मुमोचतुस्तौ सुभृशं हि कोपात् ॥
7.m: A hundred Nara, three hundred the Daitya; six the son of Dharma, ten the Daitya king; / then both of them furiously shot even more countless arrows out of rage.

7.s:
tato naro bāṇagaṇairasakhyairavāstaradbhūmimatho diśaḥ kham /
sa cāpi daityapravaraḥ pṛṣatkaiściccheda vegāt tapanīyapuṅkhaiḥ //
7.d:
ततो नरो बाणगणैरसख्यैरवास्तरद्भूमिमथो दिशः खम् ।
स चापि दैत्यप्रवरः पृषत्कैश्चिच्छेद वेगात् तपनीयपुङ्खैः ॥
7.m: Then with countless throngs of arrows Nara covered the earth, the directions, and the sky; / and that foremost Daitya swiftly cut [them] down with gold-feathered shafts.

7.s:
tataḥ patattribhirvīrau subhṛśaṃ naradānavau /
yuddhe varāstrairyudhyetāṃ ghorarūpaiḥ parasparam //
7.d:
ततः पतत्त्रिभिर्वीरौ सुभृशं नरदानवौ ।
युद्धे वरास्त्रैर्युध्येतां घोररूपैः परस्परम् ॥
7.m: Then with winged [arrows] those two heroes, the man and the Dānava, / fought one another furiously in battle with dreadful, choice missiles.

7.s:
tatastu daityena varāstrapāṇinā cāpe niyuktaṃ tu pitāmahāstram /
maheśvarāstraṃ puruṣottameva samaṃ samāhatya nipetatustau //
7.d:
ततस्तु दैत्येन वरास्त्रपाणिना चापे नियुक्तं तु पितामहास्त्रम् ।
महेश्वरास्त्रं पुरुषोत्तमेव समं समाहत्य निपेततुस्तौ ॥
7.m: Then the Daitya, holding a choice missile in hand, discharged the missile of Pitāmaha from his bow; / the Puruṣottama [discharged] the missile of Maheśvara; striking together, the two [missiles] fell.

7.s:
brahmastre tu praśamite prahlādaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ /
gadāṃ pragṛhya tarasā pracaskanda rathottamāt //
7.d:
ब्रह्मस्त्रे तु प्रशमिते प्रह्लादः क्रोधमूर्छितः ।
गदां प्रगृह्य तरसा प्रचस्कन्द रथोत्तमात् ॥
7.m: When the missile of Brahmā was neutralized, Prahlāda, fainting with rage, / grasped a mace and swiftly sprang down from his excellent chariot.

7.s:
gadāpāṇiṃ samāyāntaṃ daityaṃ nārāyaṇastadā /
dṛṣṭvātha pṛṣṭhataścakre naraṃ yoddhūmanāḥ svayam //
7.d:
गदापाणिं समायान्तं दैत्यं नारायणस्तदा ।
दृष्ट्वाथ पृष्ठतश्चक्रे नरं योद्धूमनाः स्वयम् ॥
7.m: Seeing the Daitya approaching with mace in hand, Nārāyaṇa then / placed Nara behind him, wishing to fight himself.

7.s:
tato dītīśaḥ sagadaḥ samādravat saśārṅgapāṇiṃ tapasāṃ nidhānam /
khyātaṃ purāṇarṣimudāravikramaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ nārada lokapālam //
iti śrīvāmanapurāṇe saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ
7.d:
ततो दीतीशः सगदः समाद्रवत् सशार्ङ्गपाणिं तपसां निधानम् ।
ख्यातं पुराणर्षिमुदारविक्रमं नारायणं नारद लोकपालम् ॥
इति श्रीवामनपुराणे सप्तमो ऽध्यायः
7.m:
Then the lord of Diti's line, mace in hand, rushed at Nārāyaṇa, the world-guardian, / who held the Śārṅga in hand, was the abode of austerities, the renowned ancient sage of noble prowess, O Nārada.

Thus ends the seventh chapter in the glorious Vāmana Purāṇa.

8.s:
pulastya uvāca /
śārṅgapāṇinamāyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvāgre dānaveśvaraḥ /
paribhrāmya gadāṃ vegāt mūrdhni sādhyamatāḍayat //
8.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच ।
शार्ङ्गपाणिनमायान्तं दृष्ट्वाग्रे दानवेश्वरः ।
परिभ्राम्य गदां वेगात् मूर्ध्नि साध्यमताडयत् ॥
8.m: Pulastya said: / Seeing him approaching with the Śārṅga in hand, the lord of the Dānavas / whirled his mace with force and struck the Sādhya on the head.

8.s:
tāḍitasyātha gadayā dharmaputrasya nārada /
netrābhyāmapatad vāri vahnivarṣanibhaṃ bhuvi //
8.d:
ताडितस्याथ गदया धर्मपुत्रस्य नारद ।
नेत्राभ्यामपतद् वारि वह्निवर्षनिभं भुवि ॥
8.m: From the eyes of the son of Dharma, struck with the mace, O Nārada, / water fell to the ground like a rain of fire.

8.s:
mūrdhni nārāyaṇasyāpi sā gadā dānavārpitā /
jagāma śatadhā brahmañśailaśṛṅge yathāśaniḥ //
8.d:
मूर्ध्नि नारायणस्यापि सा गदा दानवार्पिता ।
जगाम शतधा ब्रह्मञ्शैलशृङ्गे यथाशनिः ॥
8.m: And that mace hurled by the Dānava onto the head of Nārāyaṇa / shattered into a hundred pieces, O Brahmin, like a thunderbolt on a mountain peak.

8.s:
tato nivṛtya daityendraḥ samāsthāya rathaṃ drutam /
ādāya kārmukaṃ vīrastūṇad bāṇaṃ samādade //
8.d:
ततो निवृत्य दैत्येन्द्रः समास्थाय रथं द्रुतम् ।
आदाय कार्मुकं वीरस्तूणद् बाणं समाददे ॥
8.m: Then the lord of the Daityas, turning back, swiftly mounted his chariot; / taking up his bow, the hero drew an arrow from his quiver.

8.s:
ānamya cāpaṃ vegena gārddhūpatrāñsilīmukhān /
mumoca sādhyāya tadā krodhandhakāritānanaḥ //
8.d:
आनम्य चापं वेगेन गार्द्धूपत्राञ्सिलीमुखान् ।
मुमोच साध्याय तदा क्रोधन्धकारिताननः ॥
8.m: Bending the bow with speed, his face darkened with anger, / he then released vulture-feathered arrows at the Sādhya.

8.s:
tānāpatata evāśu bāṇāṃścandrārddhasannibhān /
ciccheda bāṇairaparairnirbibheda ca dānavam //
8.d:
तानापतत एवाशु बाणांश्चन्द्रार्द्धसन्निभान् ।
चिच्छेद बाणैरपरैर्निर्बिभेद च दानवम् ॥
8.m: Even as those crescent-shaped arrows were flying, [Nārāyaṇa] swiftly / cut them down with other arrows and pierced the Dānava.

8.s:
tato nārāyaṇaṃ daityo daityaṃ nārāyaṇaḥ śaraiḥ /
āvidhyetāṃ tadānyonyaṃ marmabhidbhirajihyagaiḥ //
8.d:
ततो नारायणं दैत्यो दैत्यं नारायणः शरैः ।
आविध्येतां तदान्योन्यं मर्मभिद्भिरजिह्यगैः ॥
8.m: Then the Daitya struck Nārāyaṇa, and Nārāyaṇa the Daitya, with straight-flying / arrows that pierced the vital spots.

8.s:
tato 'mbare saṃnipāto devānāmabhavanmune /
didṛkṣūṇāṃ tadā yuddhaṃ laghu citraṃ ca suṣṭhu ca //
8.d:
ततो ऽम्बरे संनिपातो देवानामभवन्मुने ।
दिदृक्षूणां तदा युद्धं लघु चित्रं च सुष्ठु च ॥
8.m: Then, O sage, an assembly of the gods gathered in the sky, / desiring to watch that battle, swift, wondrous, and magnificent.

8.s:
tataḥ surāṇāṃ dundubhyas tvavādyanta mahāsvanāḥ /
puṣpavarṣamanaupamyaṃ mumucuḥ sādhyadaityayauḥ //
8.d:
ततः सुराणां दुन्दुभ्यस् त्ववाद्यन्त महास्वनाः ।
पुष्पवर्षमनौपम्यं मुमुचुः साध्यदैत्ययौः ॥
8.m: Then the loud-sounding kettledrums of the gods were sounded, / and they showered an incomparable rain of flowers on the Sādhya and the Daitya.

8.s:
tataḥ paśyatsu deveṣu gaganastheṣu tāvubhau /
ayudhyetāṃ maheṣvāsau prekṣakaprītivarddhanam //
8.d:
ततः पश्यत्सु देवेषु गगनस्थेषु तावुभौ ।
अयुध्येतां महेष्वासौ प्रेक्षकप्रीतिवर्द्धनम् ॥
8.m: Then, while the gods stood looking on in the sky, both of them, / mighty archers, fought, increasing the delight of the onlookers.

8.s:
babandhatustadākāśaṃ tāvubhau śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ /
diśaśca vidiśaścaiva chādayetāṃ śarotkaraiḥ //
8.d:
बबन्धतुस्तदाकाशं तावुभौ शरवृष्टिभिः ।
दिशश्च विदिशश्चैव छादयेतां शरोत्करैः ॥
8.m: Both of them bound the sky with showers of arrows, / and covered the cardinal and intermediate directions with heaps of shafts.

8.s:
tato nārāyaṇaścāpaṃ samākṛṣya mahāmune /
bibheda mārgaṇaistīkṣṇaiḥ prahlādaṃ sarvamarmasu //
8.d:
ततो नारायणश्चापं समाकृष्य महामुने ।
बिभेद मार्गणैस्तीक्ष्णैः प्रह्लादं सर्वमर्मसु ॥
8.m: Then, O great sage, Nārāyaṇa drew his bow / and pierced Prahlāda in all his vital spots with sharp shafts.

8.s:
tathā daityeśvaraḥ kruddhaścāpamānamya vegavān /
bibheda hṛdaye bāhvorvadane ca narottamam //
8.d:
तथा दैत्येश्वरः क्रुद्धश्चापमानम्य वेगवान् ।
बिभेद हृदये बाह्वोर्वदने च नरोत्तमम् ॥
8.m: Likewise the lord of the Daityas, enraged and swift, bent his bow / and pierced that best of men in the chest, arms, and face.

8.s:
tato 'syato daityapateḥ kārmukaṃ muṣṭibandhanāt /
cicchedaikena bāṇena candrārdhākāravarcasā //
8.d:
ततो ऽस्यतो दैत्यपतेः कार्मुकं मुष्टिबन्धनात् ।
चिच्छेदैकेन बाणेन चन्द्रार्धाकारवर्चसा ॥
8.m: Then, as the lord of the Daityas was shooting, [Nārāyaṇa] severed his bow at the grip / with a single arrow shining like the half-moon.

8.s:
apāsyata dhanuśchinnaṃ cāpamādāya cāparam /
adhijyaṃ lāghavāt kṛtvā vavarṣa niśitāñśarān //
8.d:
अपास्यत धनुश्छिन्नं चापमादाय चापरम् ।
अधिज्यं लाघवात् कृत्वा ववर्ष निशिताञ्शरान् ॥
8.m: Casting aside the broken bow, he took up another, / strung it with agility, and rained down sharp arrows.

8.s:
tānapyasya śarān sādhyaśchittvā bāṇairavārayat /
kārmukaṃ ca kṣurapreṇa ciccheda puruṣottamaḥ //
8.d:
तानप्यस्य शरान् साध्यश्छित्त्वा बाणैरवारयत् ।
कार्मुकं च क्षुरप्रेण चिच्छेद पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
8.m: Cutting down those arrows of his as well, the Sādhya repelled them with shafts, / and the Puruṣottama severed his bow with a razor-headed arrow.

8.s:
chinnaṃ chinnaṃ dhanurdaityastvanyadanyatsamādade /
samādattaṃ tadā sādhyo mune ciccheda lāghavāt //
8.d:
छिन्नं छिन्नं धनुर्दैत्यस्त्वन्यदन्यत्समाददे ।
समादत्तं तदा साध्यो मुने चिच्छेद लाघवात् ॥
8.m: As each bow was severed, the Daitya seized another and yet another; / as each was seized, O sage, the Sādhya severed it with agility.

8.s:
saṃchinneṣvatha cāpeṣu jagrāha ditijeśvaraḥ /
parighaṃ dāruṇāṃ dīrghaṃ sarvalohamayaṃ dṛḍham //
8.d:
संछिन्नेष्वथ चापेषु जग्राह दितिजेश्वरः ।
परिघं दारुणां दीर्घं सर्वलोहमयं दृढम् ॥
8.m: When his bows were completely shattered, the lord of Diti's sons seized / a dreadful, long iron club, solid and entirely of metal.

8.s:
parigṛhyātha parighaṃ bhrāmayāmāsa dānavaḥ /
bhrāmyamāṇaṃ sa ciccheda nārācena mahāmuniḥ //
8.d:
परिगृह्याथ परिघं भ्रामयामास दानवः ।
भ्राम्यमाणं स चिच्छेद नाराचेन महामुनिः ॥
8.m: Taking up the iron club, the Dānava whirled it around; / and as it was being whirled, the great sage sliced it with an iron arrow.

8.s:
chinne tu parighe śrīmān prahlādo dānaveśvaraḥ /
mudgaraṃ bhrāmya vegena pracikṣepa narāgraje //
8.d:
छिन्ने तु परिघे श्रीमान् प्रह्लादो दानवेश्वरः ।
मुद्गरं भ्राम्य वेगेन प्रचिक्षेप नराग्रजे ॥
8.m: When the iron club was cut, the glorious Prahlāda, lord of the Dānavas, / spun a mallet with speed and hurled it at the elder brother of Nara.

8.s:
tamāpatantaṃ balavān mārgaṇairdaśabhirmune /
ciccheda daśadhā sādhyaḥ sa chinno nyapatad bhuvi //
8.d:
तमापतन्तं बलवान् मार्गणैर्दशभिर्मुने ।
चिच्छेद दशधा साध्यः स छिन्नो न्यपतद् भुवि ॥
8.m: O sage, as it came flying, the powerful Sādhya cut it / ten times into ten pieces with arrows; cut to pieces, it fell to the earth.

8.s:
mudgare vitathe jāte prāsamāvidhya vegavān /
pracikṣepa narāgryāya taṃ ca ciccheda dharmajaḥ //
8.d:
मुद्गरे वितथे जाते प्रासमाविध्य वेगवान् ।
प्रचिक्षेप नराग्र्याय तं च चिच्छेद धर्मजः ॥
8.m: When the mallet was rendered useless, he twirled a dart with swiftness / and hurled it at the best of men; and the son of Dharma cut it down.

8.s:
prāse chinne tato daityaḥ śaktimādāya cikṣipe /
tāṃ ca ciccheda balavān kṣurapreṇa mahātapāḥ //
8.d:
प्रासे छिन्ने ततो दैत्यः शक्तिमादाय चिक्षिपे ।
तां च चिच्छेद बलवान् क्षुरप्रेण महातपाः ॥
8.m: When the dart was cut, the Daitya then took a spear and hurled it; / and the powerful one of great austerities cut it with a crescent-headed arrow.

8.s:
chinneṣu teṣu śastreṣu dānavo 'nyanmahaddhanuḥ /
samādāya tato bāṇairavatastāra nārada //
8.d:
छिन्नेषु तेषु शस्त्रेषु दानवो ऽन्यन्महद्धनुः ।
समादाय ततो बाणैरवतस्तार नारद ॥
8.m: When those weapons were cut, the Dānava took another great bow, / and then covered him with arrows, O Nārada.

8.s:
tato nārāyaṇo devo daityanāthaṃ jagadguruḥ /
nārācena jaghānātha hṛdaye suratāpasaḥ //
8.d:
ततो नारायणो देवो दैत्यनाथं जगद्गुरुः ।
नाराचेन जघानाथ हृदये सुरतापसः ॥
8.m: Then the divine Nārāyaṇa, the guru of the universe and ascetic among gods, / struck the Daitya chief in the heart with an iron arrow.

8.s:
saṃbhinnihṛdayo brahman devenādbhutakarmaṇā /
nipapāta rathopasthe tamapovāha sārathiḥ //
8.d:
संभिन्निहृदयो ब्रह्मन् देवेनाद्भुतकर्मणा ।
निपपात रथोपस्थे तमपोवाह सारथिः ॥
8.m: His heart pierced, O Brahmin, by the god of wondrous deeds, / he collapsed on the chariot-box, and his charioteer carried him away.

8.s:
sa saṃjñāṃ sucireṇaiva pratilabhya ditīśvaraḥ /
sudṛḍhaṃ cāpamādāya bhūyo yoddhamupāgataḥ //
8.d:
स संज्ञां सुचिरेणैव प्रतिलभ्य दितीश्वरः ।
सुदृढं चापमादाय भूयो योद्धमुपागतः ॥
8.m: Regaining consciousness after a long time, the lord of Diti's line / took up a very strong bow and approached once more to fight.

8.s:
tamāgataṃ saṃnirīkṣya pratyuvāca narāgrajaḥ /
gaccha daityendra yotsyāmaḥ prātastvāhnikamācara //
8.d:
तमागतं संनिरीक्ष्य प्रत्युवाच नराग्रजः ।
गच्छ दैत्येन्द्र योत्स्यामः प्रातस्त्वाह्निकमाचर ॥
8.m: Beholding him approached, the elder brother of Nara replied to him: / 'Go, Daitya Indra; we will fight in the morning; perform your daily rites.'

8.s:
evamukto ditīśastu sādhyenādbhutakarmaṇā /
jagāma naimiṣāraṇyaṃ kriyāṃ cakre tadā'hnikīm //
8.d:
एवमुक्तो दितीशस्तु साध्येनाद्भुतकर्मणा ।
जगाम नैमिषारण्यं क्रियां चक्रे तदाऽह्निकीम् ॥
8.m: Thus spoken to by the Sādhya of wondrous deeds, the lord of Diti's line / went to the Naimiṣa forest and then performed his daily rites.

8.s:
evaṃ yudhyati deve ca prahlādo hyasuro mune /
rātrau cintayate yuddhe kathaṃ jeṣyāmi dāmbhikam //
8.d:
एवं युध्यति देवे च प्रह्लादो ह्यसुरो मुने ।
रात्रौ चिन्तयते युद्धे कथं जेष्यामि दाम्भिकम् ॥
8.m: As the god thus fought, the asura Prahlāda, O sage, / reflected at night during the battle: 'How shall I conquer this deceitful one?'

8.s:
evaṃ nārāyaṇenāsau sahāyudhyata nārada /
divyaṃ varṣasasraṃ tu daityo devaṃ na cājayat //
8.d:
एवं नारायणेनासौ सहायुध्यत नारद ।
दिव्यं वर्षसस्रं तु दैत्यो देवं न चाजयत् ॥
8.m: In this manner he fought together with Nārāyaṇa, O Nārada, / for a thousand divine years, yet the Daitya could not vanquish the god.

8.s:
tato varṣasahasrānte hyajite puruṣottame /
pītavāsasamabhyetya dānavo vākyamabravīt //
8.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रान्ते ह्यजिते पुरुषोत्तमे ।
पीतवाससमभ्येत्य दानवो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
8.m: Then, at the end of the thousand years, the Puruṣottama being unconquered, / the Dānava approached the Yellow-Robed One and spoke these words:

8.s:
kimarthaṃ devadeveśa sādhyaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim /
vijetuṃ nādya śaknomi etanme kāraṇaṃ vada //
8.d:
किमर्थं देवदेवेश साध्यं नारायणं हरिम् ।
विजेतुं नाद्य शक्नोमि एतन्मे कारणं वद ॥
8.m: 'For what reason, O lord of the gods of gods, can I not conquer today / the Sādhya Nārāyaṇa, Hari? Tell me the reason for this.'

8.s:
pītavāsā uvāca /
durjayo 'sau mahābāhustvayā prahlāda dharmajaḥ /
sādhyo vipravaro dhīmān mṛdhe devāsurairapi //
8.d:
पीतवासा उवाच ।
दुर्जयो ऽसौ महाबाहुस्त्वया प्रह्लाद धर्मजः ।
साध्यो विप्रवरो धीमान् मृधे देवासुरैरपि ॥
8.m: The Yellow-Robed One said: / 'O Prahlāda, this mighty-armed son of Dharma is invincible to you in battle, / the Sādhya, the best among Brahmins, the wise, even by gods and asuras.'

8.s:
prahlāda uvāca /
yadyasau durjayo deva mayā sādhyo raṇājire /
tatkathaṃ yatpratijñātaṃ tadasatyaṃ bhaviṣyati //
8.d:
प्रह्लाद उवाच ।
यद्यसौ दुर्जयो देव मया साध्यो रणाजिरे ।
तत्कथं यत्प्रतिज्ञातं तदसत्यं भविष्यति ॥
8.m: Prahlāda said: / 'If this Sādhya is invincible to me on the battlefield, O god, / then how can it be that what was pledged will become false?

8.s:
hīnapratijño deveśa kathaṃ jīveta mādṛśaḥ /
tasmāttavāgrato viṣṇo kariṣye kāyaśodhanam //
8.d:
हीनप्रतिज्ञो देवेश कथं जीवेत मादृशः ।
तस्मात्तवाग्रतो विष्णो करिष्ये कायशोधनम् ॥
